built.subject: from 5e8340e: Phase 6 under D-2, the governance lanes, the holder, the four laws

assumed.subject: Trigger text never enters the chain
assumed.summary: Chose: Trigger.as_dict() (the chain view) excludes text; spec/event.schema.json's trigger object has only kind and source.
assumed.body:
**Chose:** `Trigger.as_dict()` (the chain view) excludes `text`; `spec/event.schema.json`'s `trigger` object has only `kind` and `source`.
**Over:** leaving `text` on `activation.started`, which is what the runtime was doing.
**Because:** a new CLI regression test (`tests/test_cli.py`) caught `activate --text "…"` writing the raw text into the immutable log — the same content-in-chain leak that had already been removed from messages and memories. Found by test, not by review; that is the argument for the test.
**Reversal cost:** cheap technically, but reversing it would break the deletion guarantee (§15.1) — do not.
**Depends on:** the no-content-in-the-chain invariant (2026-09-03).

assumed.subject: The analysis boundary is a code gate, not a policy
assumed.summary: Chose: runtime/agent_society/analysis/ — every study result leaves through release(), which refuses any string that is not an id, hash, DID, timestamp, model ref, event kind or closed-enum value.
assumed.body:
**Chose:** `runtime/agent_society/analysis/` — every study result leaves through `release()`, which refuses any string that is not an id, hash, DID, timestamp, model ref, event kind or closed-enum value. A memory's text in a summary raises `ContentLeak` before a human sees it. `leakage_check()` takes sealed instrument text *in* and returns only booleans and overlap scores.
**Over:** a written rule that people won't read content.
**Because:** the data-access decision (automated analysis, no human reading) has to be true in the code for the consent form to be honest.
**Reversal cost:** moderate — participants consent to this shape.

assumed.subject: Channel adapters are dumb pipes; the bridge routes
assumed.summary: Chose: runtime/agent_society/channels/ — Telegram (Bot API long-poll, httpx) and email (IMAP/SMTP, stdlib) transports that only poll and send; a Bridge that dedupes on the channel's own message id, resolves (channel, chat) → agent DID through a bindings table, runs Runtime.chat, and sends replies.
assumed.body:
**Chose:** `runtime/agent_society/channels/` — Telegram (Bot API long-poll, `httpx`) and email (IMAP/SMTP, stdlib) transports that only poll and send; a `Bridge` that dedupes on the channel's own message id, resolves `(channel, chat) → agent DID` through a bindings table, runs `Runtime.chat`, and sends replies. Unbound chats get one hint and nothing else. A dead transport never stops the other.
**Over:** a Telegram-specific bot with routing logic inside it.
**Because:** both channels to every participant, recorded per message as a covariate — so the channel must be interchangeable at the edge.
**Open:** `Runtime.chat(channel=…)` is not threaded through yet; the bridge falls back to the Month-1 signature until it is.

assumed.subject: permission.decision carries the action's chain view only
assumed.summary: Chose: the event payload holds action: {kind, domain, tool?} plus decision_id, requested_level, decision, reason, escalation_of — exactly spec/event.schema.json.
assumed.body:
**Chose:** the event payload holds `action: {kind, domain, tool?}` plus `decision_id`, `requested_level`, `decision`, `reason`, `escalation_of` — exactly `spec/event.schema.json`. The drafted text and params stay on the off-chain `approvals` row, which is where a human reviews them.
**Over:** what the runtime did — `action.as_dict()` with the model's full drafted reply welded into the signed chain on every escalation.
**Because:** jarvis11's review found it; conformance never had, because the fake provider's actions are always allowed so no escalation event was ever validated. For a human-subjects study this was the worst of the content leaks: the model's draft *to a participant*, undeletable.
**Reversal cost:** do not reverse; it would break the deletion guarantee.

assumed.subject: Inbound email is external_untrusted until the sender is bound
assumed.summary: Chose: Runtime.source_kind_for_channel() — CLI, Telegram, web, API and the harness probe channel write principal messages as stated_by_principal; email writes them as external_untrusted.
assumed.body:
**Chose:** `Runtime.source_kind_for_channel()` — CLI, Telegram, web, API and the harness probe channel write principal messages as `stated_by_principal`; **email writes them as `external_untrusted`.**
**Over:** treating every channel's "this is the principal" claim as equal.
**Because:** an email `From:` header is forgeable and the bridge routes on it. Worse than one injected belief: a spoofed `stated_by_principal` memory ranks highest in `spec/source-classes.md` and could serve as *corroboration* to promote other untrusted content — a poisoning path rule 4 exists to block. Telegram's chat id is platform-authenticated; email's is not.
**Open:** a bind-time secret (the operator issues a code at binding; the first email must carry it) would let verified email senders be upgraded. Not built yet.
**Reversal cost:** cheap — one mapping.

assumed.subject: For the synthetic arm, the reveal map is the leakage authority
assumed.summary: Chose: harness/synthetic/score.py computes the leakage-adjusted preference score from reveal-map.yaml (ground truth by construction: which items were *never* stated), and only cross-checks against analysis.leakage_check.
assumed.body:
**Chose:** `harness/synthetic/score.py` computes the leakage-adjusted preference score from `reveal-map.yaml` (ground truth by construction: which items were *never* stated), and only cross-checks against `analysis.leakage_check`.
**Over:** using `leakage_check`'s word-overlap for both arms.
**Because:** building the arm surfaced a real false positive — a held-out personal dilemma scored as "leaked" (overlap 0.53) because it shared proper nouns (a person, a company) with unrelated stated facts. Word overlap on short texts with shared names is not a reliable leakage test. For **real** participants there is no reveal map, so `leakage_check` remains the only tool there; its threshold and this failure mode must be reported as a limitation in the analysis plan.
**Reversal cost:** cheap — but do not silently switch the real arm to a reveal map that does not exist.

assumed.subject: Corrections are metadata beside a memory, not a field on it
assumed.summary: Chose: a corrections table (agent_id, memory_id, review_activation_id, created_at).
assumed.body:
**Chose:** a `corrections` table (`agent_id, memory_id, review_activation_id, created_at`). A principal message that follows a `weekly_review` activation is written as a normal `stated_by_principal` memory whose `source_ref` points at that review, plus one correction row. The weekly correction rate is released through the analysis boundary as `memory.corrections`.
**Over:** a boolean on the memory record.
**Because:** the memory record is signed and its schema is closed (`additionalProperties: false`); a correction is a fact *about* a memory, so it belongs beside it, and the signed record stays exactly what the participant's agent wrote.
**Also decided:** the daily check-in (`trigger.source == "checkin"`, default 18:00) and weekly review (`weekly_review`, default Sunday) are scheduled activations whose prompts are the verbatim text of `harness/instrument/daily-checkin.md` / `weekly-review.md`; the open-commitments list and the belief summary the agent presents are **computed by the runtime from the facts table**, never by the model.
**Reversal cost:** cheap.

assumed.subject: Guard reviews get a standing trigger, not an ad-hoc invitation
assumed.summary: Chose: a project PostToolUse hook (.claude/settings.json → .claude/hooks/review-reminder.py) that, after any Edit/Write under runtime/agent_society/{loop,policy,memory,gateway,api}/, spec/, or eventlog/identity, prints one line naming which guard (jarvis11: enforcement surfaces; jarvis22: spec/payload contract) is pending before commit.
assumed.body:
**Chose:** a project `PostToolUse` hook (`.claude/settings.json` → `.claude/hooks/review-reminder.py`) that, after any Edit/Write under `runtime/agent_society/{loop,policy,memory,gateway,api}/`, `spec/`, or `eventlog/identity`, prints one line naming which guard (jarvis11: enforcement surfaces; jarvis22: spec/payload contract) is pending before commit. Reminder only — it never spawns an agent.
**Over:** auto-spawning the guards on every edit (expensive, noisy) or relying on remembering to invite them (Tom's finding: four of eight failures this session were exactly their class, all caught late).
**Because:** `docs/LESSONS.md` 2026-09-04, "one change to make before the next session".
**Reversal cost:** trivial — delete the hook.

assumed.subject: The world map is a gazetteer, not a mural
assumed.summary: Chose: every building in docs/harbor-of-record.html stands for one register the world engine is authoritative for (or one runtime module), keeps a live ledger, and is documented in docs/world/GAZETTEER.md with its white-paper section and runtime module.
assumed.body:
**Chose:** every building in `docs/harbor-of-record.html` stands for one register the world engine is authoritative for (or one runtime module), keeps a live ledger, and is documented in `docs/world/GAZETTEER.md` with its white-paper section and runtime module. Nine municipal institutions were added on that rule — Mint (RESOURCES as a compute credit, the *mark*), Cadastre (LOCATION as tenancy), Athenaeum (attested knowledge; `counterparty_signed` and above, never `external_untrusted`), Tribunal (disputes), Assay Office (REPUTATION), Customs House (source-class quarantine), Infirmary (key rotation), Necropolis (tombstones, outside the wall), Foundry (the models, on an island offshore because engines are suppliers, not institutions).
**Over:** decorative buildings with no state.
**Because:** the principal asked for a world where "each building has a function". The map is only worth keeping if it teaches the architecture; a building without a register is a lie about the system.
**Reversal cost:** trivial (a web page), but any new building must name its register first.

---

assumed.subject: Reach means *research* reach — the publishable-result decision is amplified, not reversed
assumed.summary: Chose: Exp. 8 stays the deliverable.
assumed.body:
**Chose:** Exp. 8 stays the deliverable. The spec ships as a reproducibility artifact plus one cheap, falsifiable adoption test.
**Over:** reopening "open standard + reference runtime" as the primary goal.
**Because:** a 2026 literature scan found the *protocol* half of the contribution already published by others — arXiv 2605.11032 (Portable Agent Memory: cryptographically-verified transfer, Merkle-DAG provenance, capability access control, Python SDK) and 2604.09588 (soul.py, multi-anchor persistent identity), both verified. **Neither has participants, duration, blinding or statistics.** The evidence half is unoccupied; the nearest human-subjects ancestor is Migratable AI (2010.13319, 2020), which studies embodiment migration, not model replacement.
**Consequences:** lead with evidence; cite 2605.11032 as related work; stop treating the format as novel. Phases 3–4 stay unbuilt. §12's second implementation, federation design and registry listings stay deferred.
**Reversal cost:** cheap — it is a framing, and the artifacts serve both readings.
**Depends on:** "Success is a publishable research result" (2026-09-04), which this amplifies.

assumed.subject: The scarce resource is pre-day-0 lead time and participant-weeks, not money or the 90 days
assumed.summary: Chose: treat reach work as two classes — *participant-surface* (must be settled before day 0 or deferred past day 90) and *non-participant-surface* (near-free, and it consumes the dead weeks anyway).
assumed.body:
**Chose:** treat reach work as two classes — *participant-surface* (must be settled before day 0 or deferred past day 90) and *non-participant-surface* (near-free, and it consumes the dead weeks anyway).
**Over:** planning reach against budget or against the 90-day clock.
**Because:** money is not a constraint ($0.11–0.17/agent-day, clearing the §17 target 3–4×). The 90 days is irreducible but *known*. The variance is upstream — ethics 0–8 weeks, recruiting 2–6 weeks — and none of it compresses with more tokens or more agents.
**Consequence — currently unaddressed in the plan:** attrition, not delay, is the largest threat. A 90-day daily commitment from unpaid volunteers loses 30–50%, so **15 recruits plausibly yields 8, not 10**. Retention design before day 0 buys more than starting two weeks earlier.
**Reversal cost:** cheap as a framing; expensive as a consequence — retention design not done before day 0 cannot be retrofitted mid-study.
**Depends on:** n=10 (recruit 15); channel decision; ethics posture (still open).
**[friday22 note]** The n=10 decision's stated reasoning was that N is not the binding constraint, bias is. A yield of 8 does not threaten that argument. But 8 was never the number the pre-registration was written against — if this holds, `harness/PREREGISTRATION.md` should say 8–10 before recruiting, not after.

assumed.subject: Experiment A — an adoption analogue of Exp. 8, pre-registered, able to return NO
assumed.summary: Chose: pre-register an adoption hypothesis with thresholds and a stop rule.
assumed.body:
**Chose:** pre-register an adoption hypothesis with thresholds and a stop rule. H: independent developers will run a conformance suite against their own implementation. At 30 days: ≥3 distinct non-team parties run it, ≥1 files a substantive spec issue, ≥1 states intent to implement.
**Over:** publishing the spec and inferring adoption from impressions.
**Because:** the project falsifies its central claim cheaply rather than assuming it; adoption deserves the same discipline and currently does not get it. Fail → stop the universality track, which merely confirms the standing decision, at ~$100.
**Reversal cost:** cheap.
**Depends on:** a licence and a public repo (both open); the conformance suite (done).

assumed.subject: Experiment 11 — governance evidence
assumed.summary: Chose: run a GateMem-style evaluation (arXiv 2606.18829, June 2026 — utility + access control + active forgetting) against the runtime.
assumed.body:
**Chose:** run a GateMem-style evaluation (arXiv 2606.18829, June 2026 — utility + access control + active forgetting) against the runtime.
**Over:** asserting the architectural claim without a benchmark.
**Because:** GateMem reports that **no** method it tested achieves all three, and every one of them asks the *model* to respect deletion and access control. Design rules 1 and 6 mean this architecture never does — that is a testable claim, and it is compute-bound, not calendar-bound, so it runs inside the study window at zero calendar cost.
**Recorded caveat:** GateMem is multi-principal shared-memory; this project is single-principal-per-agent, so the shapes may not transfer. **A negative result is informative and must be reported.**
**Reversal cost:** cheap.
**Depends on:** design rules 1 and 6; the analysis boundary.

assumed.subject: The world has a live mode, and the crier is not the record
assumed.summary: Chose: docs/harbor-of-record.html?api=<url> pulls real agents from GET /agents and their chain from GET /world/events and GET /agents/{id}/chain; real citizens carry their real DID, level and model binding, and the Archive shows the runtime's own chain verdict.
assumed.body:
**Chose:** `docs/harbor-of-record.html?api=<url>` pulls real agents from `GET /agents` and their chain from `GET /world/events` and `GET /agents/{id}/chain`; real citizens carry their real DID, level and model binding, and the Archive shows the runtime's own chain verdict. Verified end to end against `agent-society serve` (a real agent appeared as a citizen; its chain verified). The town crier under the map states events in plain words and is labelled "never the record": the log keeps kinds, actors and hashes only.
**Over:** a purely decorative map, or a crier that quoted message text.
**Because:** the map is worth keeping only if it can show the real system; and the crier/record contrast teaches the no-content-in-the-chain rule better than a paragraph does.
**Reversal cost:** trivial.
**Depends on:** the HTTP API (2026-09-04), the no-content invariant (2026-09-03).

assumed.subject: did:web is an alias, never authority; our passport rides an A2A Agent Card as an extension
assumed.summary: Chose: identity stays did:key.
assumed.body:
**Chose:** identity stays `did:key`. A hosted agent may carry `alsoKnownAs: [did:web:<host>[%3A<port>]:agents:<msid>]`, resolved per the W3C did:web method to `/agents/<msid>/did.json`, which returns the same signed passport as `/agents/<did>/passport.json`. A verifier must check that the resolved document's `id` and every verificationMethod controller equal the expected `did:key`, that the proof verifies, and that the alias is claimed in `alsoKnownAs` — the alias adds reachability and nothing else. `/.well-known/agent-passport.json` is an **unsigned directory** (trust comes from each passport's own proof). Service endpoints change only by a signed `service.updated` event. For interoperability the agent also serves a standard A2A v1.0 Agent Card carrying our extension `https://agentsociety.org/ext/agent-passport/v0` with params `{did, passport, historyHead}` — "publish an extension profile", not a parallel convention. Ours is the *Agent Passport*; A2A's differently named example extension is a different object and the profile says so.
**Over:** making did:web the identity (would tie the agent to a host — the captivity §15.2 forbids); a signed index (a directory is not a claim); a bespoke well-known shape that litellm's existing A2A card resolver could not read.
**Because:** ROADMAP §12 row 1 ("passport hosting that does not depend on us"), the reach-landscape scan §4 (A2A 1.0 signed cards, extension mechanism, litellm resolver in our dependency tree).
**Reversal cost:** cheap for the card and index shapes; expensive if did:web were ever allowed to carry authority.
**Depends on:** ADR-005 (did:key now), the no-content-in-the-chain invariant (endpoints are metadata).

assumed.subject: Living World: what happens at the counter when the agent cannot pay
assumed.summary: Chose: in city/ (Living World Phase 1, Halvik), every household purchase and rent passes the agent layer's authorize() first, and the outcome is read as a statement about the *agent*, not the human: allow → the agent settles it; escalate → the principal is standing at the counter and answers on the spot, paying themselves (audited as human-present); deny citing a mandate → the delegation says no, nothing is paid; deny with no mandate at all → a gap in what was delegated, so the principal pays and the log says the agent could not.
assumed.body:
**Chose:** in `city/` (Living World Phase 1, Halvik), every household purchase and rent passes the agent layer's `authorize()` first, and the outcome is read as a statement about the *agent*, not the human: `allow` → the agent settles it; `escalate` → the principal is standing at the counter and answers on the spot, paying themselves (audited as human-present); `deny` **citing a mandate** → the delegation says no, nothing is paid; `deny` with **no mandate at all** → a gap in what was delegated, so the principal pays and the log says the agent could not. Every outcome reaches the hash-chained audit log.
**Over:** the strict reading (any non-`allow` blocks the money), which was implemented first and measured: the ~10 % of principals at delegation posture 0 spent the week unable to buy bread or medicine because every purchase escalated and the answer arrived after they had gone home.
**Because:** rule 5 ("no purchase without a mandate") governs *agent* purchases; a principal buying in person is rule 4's "human present" case. This keeps the mandate objects meaningful without starving the city while the standing-mandate policy is still one category wide (`grocery`).
**Reversal cost:** cheap — one function in `market.ts`/`housing.ts`; the audit log already distinguishes the cases.
**Depends on:** the v2 brief's rules 4, 5, 7, 8 (2026-09-05) and the Phase-4 economy (`42fc07f`). Argued at length in `city/DESIGN_NOTES.md`.

assumed.subject: Living World Phase 3: three planning decisions
assumed.summary: (a) Cross-border wholesale carries no mandate yet.
assumed.body:
**(a) Cross-border wholesale carries no mandate yet.** Firm-to-firm trade between Dorsk and Halvik is engine-settled with actor = nobody, exactly as domestic wholesale already is (`logistics.ts`); the trade inspector says so in words. **Over:** inventing a procurement mandate now. **Because:** the counter-seam decision governs households at a counter; no household crosses a border before migration (Phase 5); mandates for firms arrive with rules 10–13 in Phase 6. **Reversal cost:** cheap.
**(b) Lockstep at the world hour.** City workers hold at tick 60h+59 until the world's instruction for h+1 arrives; the world applies reports in ascending CityId only when all are present. This **supersedes** the Phase-0 note "the world worker never waits" (`city/DESIGN_NOTES_V2.md` §2) for Phases 3–6. **Over:** free-running workers with a recorded arrival schedule. **Because:** without lockstep two browser runs cannot produce the same hash, and a fresh run has nothing to replay; the in-process bench is the same pure function under either answer. Free-running returns in Phase 7 when tier-2 cities exist. **Reversal cost:** moderate — only the worker plumbing (D4–D6) changes. *This one contradicts an earlier design note and should be confirmed by the principal.*
**(c) The Nordholm–Veyra FTA is a zero tariff on every HS group;** the rest-of-world import backstop pays MFN from `tariffs/NLD`. **Because:** brief §3.1. **Reversal cost:** a number.
**Depends on:** Phase 2 (`a6fedc9`), the v2 brief §2–3.

assumed.subject: Living World Phase 3, integration gate: two engine fixes the lanes did not make
assumed.summary: (a) The customs yard and border depot are a map invariant.
assumed.body:
**(a) The customs yard and border depot are a map invariant.** If the district list fails to place either, the map tries every district in a fixed preference order before giving up. **Over:** accepting a city without a yard (which is what the federation's seeds produced, silently). **Because:** a city with no yard cannot receive a shipment, so every import order sat at "booked" for ten thousand ticks and the Phase 3 acceptance test could never pass. **Reversal cost:** a block in `city/src/sim/map/buildings.ts`; the single-city seed-42 map was unaffected.
**(b) A produced unit carries only the labour that went into it.** `produce()` no longer charges a whole shift's wages to the few units made before an input ran out; the idle hours stay on the payroll as the firm's loss. **Over:** widening validate's ±25 % price band, which the failure was pressing for. **Because:** the spike was bookkeeping, not scarcity — the markup rule already prices scarcity — and it compounded down a three-stage chain into a 38.6 % basket rise. **Reversal cost:** one line in `city/src/sim/systems/economy/labour.ts` and a hash re-pin. Both re-pins (city `bb5e2a01af666d57`, federation `7b9c01813505ea20`) are in the same commit, as the lane plan required.
**Depends on:** the Phase 3 planning decisions above; lanes A–D's code (`city/src/world/**`, `city/src/sim/systems/trade.ts`, `city/src/worker/world.worker.ts`). Argued in `city/DESIGN_NOTES_V2.md` §7 "integration gate".

assumed.subject: Phase 4 gate: three engine rules the fixes established, and the 3D stack the research supports
assumed.summary: Taken by the coordinator under the principal's ten-hour brief (recommended option, tagged for confirmation).
assumed.body:
Taken by the coordinator under the principal's ten-hour brief (recommended option, tagged for confirmation).
**(a) Every workplace kind a district asks for is a map invariant** — a shortfall is placed map-wide rather than dropped. **Over:** accepting a city without a farm or a mill (which the federation's Halvik map produced). **Reversal cost:** one block in `map/buildings.ts`; all three pins.
**(b) An import order is a one-hour offer.** The world reports what it booked; the city releases the rest. **Over:** orders that stand until filled (which blocked the backstop for ten days). **Reversal cost:** a field and a loop; the two federation pins.
**(c) The food chain is staffed to a floor** — half the slots of every farm, mill, bakery and grocer, filled by the nearest workers from non-food workplaces after the general matching. **Over:** leaving staffing to proximity alone (offices full, mills empty). This is an engine rule about labour, not a calibrated number; the half is `[assumed]` and belongs in `assumptions/` when lane C next runs. **Reversal cost:** one block in `population.ts`; the single-city pin.
**(d) The 3D world renderer is three.js `InstancedMesh`, buildings extruded from lane G's `KindStyle` table, assets procedural with Kenney's CC0 City Kit as licence-clean reference geometry, and a Mapbox-style smoothstep fade between the world-map and city cameras.** From solo's verification (`docs/research/intake/2026-09-06-3d-world-verified.md`): 100+ fps measured on real hardware at 2,700 static + 2,000 moving instances; Kenney's licence file opened and quoted; no maintained open-source CGA implementation exists, so building generation is our own table, not a library; Cesium-style tile streaming is the answer to unbounded real geography, which three fictional cities are not. **Over:** Babylon.js (unmeasured), a Pixi 2.5D extension (no true fly-around), Cesium/deck.gl (built for real-world tiles). **Reversal cost:** the renderer sits behind `?r=3d`; the 2D renderer stays.
**Amaranth City's price band is left failing at this gate and recorded as open** — the sea booking loop under-delivers grain to the entrepôt (32 LCs issued, 4 honoured, ships 2 % full); the fix is the next engine item, not a widened band.
**Depends on:** the Phase 4 decisions; the observatory decisions; lane G's table.

---

assumed.subject: The Isles' supply loop: four engine rules and one corrected number
assumed.summary: Taken by the coordinator while the principal was away, under their standing brief; each is tagged for confirmation.
assumed.body:
Taken by the coordinator while the principal was away, under their standing brief; each is tagged for confirmation. Argued in `city/DESIGN_NOTES_V2.md` §7 "Phase 4 — the Isles' supply loop".
**(a) A result that cannot happen must not share a value with one that merely has not happened yet.** `startExportLeg` returned `false` for both "the lorry is out" and "there is nothing to send"; the first is a wait and the second is a failure, and collapsing them lost a shipment silently. **Over:** logging the difference without acting on it. **Reversal cost:** an enum and a queue.
**(b) The price ladder's rungs describe one consignment at one moment.** The farm gate is measured where the FOB is measured — at the loading — and carried on the report, never remembered from the match and never clamped to fit. **Over:** clamping the farm gate to the FOB, which is the fabrication removed after the Phase 3 audit. **Reversal cost:** one field on the export report.
**(c) A buyer reorders against the route's lead time and against what it draws, not against its doorstep and its sales.** A mill never sells the grain it eats, so a rule built on `sold7d` read its appetite as nothing and fell back to a storage floor; that floor was survivable only because every supplier used to be minutes away. **Over:** a bigger floor, or a buffer stock for the island alone — both would have hidden the rule that was wrong for every city. **Reversal cost:** one function in `logistics.ts`; it moves all three pins, and it should.
**(d) A vessel is sized against the job the lane exists to do.** `ship_capacity_units` goes from ten truckloads to fifty, because ten was chosen for how a sailing reads on the ladder and its own justification made a claim about a city's staple demand that was never checked. **Over:** leaving it and treating the island as a special case. **Reversal cost:** one calibrated number; the `why` now carries the arithmetic.
**(e) A validation bound asserts what the design guarantees.** The freight check's "every booking sails within twice the wait bound" assumed a vessel is always within one wait of the quay, which is true only where the fleet's headway is shorter than the wait. It now asserts one headway plus the wait. **Over:** adding ships until the old bound held. **Reversal cost:** one expression in the validator.
**Result:** all three cities inside the ±25 % price band, `validate --federate` ALL CHECKS PASS over thirty days, drift 0 in three currencies, 431 tests. Pins: `42a5d72ef5139e6d` / `47153a48610947be` / `d42ed849528ae91c`. **This closes the item left open at the Phase 4 gate.**

assumed.subject: The Living World's audit chain carries a bounded reason
assumed.summary: The city's chain carries a because of at most 240 characters of plain text; for a spotlight it is a model's sentence.
assumed.body:
**The city's chain carries a `because` of at most 240 characters of plain text; for a spotlight it is a model's sentence.** It always carried an engine template; a model's sentence is new text in a hashed record. **Over:** a hash of the reason in the chain with the prose kept only on the escalation row (cleaner separation, less legible chain). **Because:** the Living World's chain is the spectator's record of *why*, and a chain that said only "reason 8a3f…" would not be one; this is not the Agent Society runtime's chain, whose "never content" rule is untouched. **Reversal cost:** one field and a re-pin of the spotlight recordings only. Argued in `city/DESIGN_NOTES_V2.md` §7 "Minds — after the architecture audit".

assumed.subject: The 3D observatory push — six routine choices
assumed.summary: Taken by the coordinator on the planner's recommendation, not put to the principal, because each is routine.
assumed.body:
Taken by the coordinator on the planner's recommendation, not put to the principal, because each is routine. Tagged for confirmation.
**(a) The observatory panel's component CSS lives in one imported file, `city/src/ui/observatory.css`** — not copied per page; two copies drift, which is the same reason the client is shared.
**(b) `3d.html` is added to `vite build` as a second input** — a page that exists only in dev is not a deliverable.

assumed.subject: No firm holds more of a good than the good survives on its shelf
assumed.summary: A firm's reorder point and its order-up-to level are capped at daily draw × shelf days, where shelf days = (100 − DAY_OLD) / stalePerDay from the goods table — bread 0.875 days, milk 2.1, vegetables 3, flour 42, wheat unbounded.
assumed.body:
**A firm's reorder point and its order-up-to level are capped at `daily draw × shelf days`, where shelf days = `(100 − DAY_OLD) / stalePerDay` from the goods table — bread 0.875 days, milk 2.1, vegetables 3, flour 42, wheat unbounded.**
**Found** tracing Halvik's grocers: the reorder floor of a tenth of the store — written for a mill's wheat — had a grocer selling eight loaves a day reorder to 300, hold five weeks of bread, throw out 190 at a time ("it had gone past selling — $2,185 written off"), and then stand at zero while the next 300 came.
**Over:** keeping the floor — a mill's wheat still needs it, and it stays for durable goods.
**Because:** a rule that orders what will rot is not a merchant's rule, and it made the bread price a function of write-offs.
**Reversal cost:** cheap — one clamp in `city/src/sim/systems/logistics.ts`; it moves the lone-city pin, which is re-pinned with this as the reason.

**Amendment (2026-09-08, after jarvis11):** the price rule reads the same shelf. Its "short" threshold is `min(SHORT_DAYS, shelf/2)` — half the shelf, the point at which a retailer of a perishable reorders, so below it the shelf is being run down, not turned over; its "overstocked" threshold is `min(OVERSTOCKED_DAYS, shelf)` — the whole shelf, which a retailer capped at the shelf never exceeds, *deliberately*: a perishable's overstock is not a markup matter, the day-old discount already cuts its price at the counter and stock past the shelf is thrown out, so the price-cut branch is for goods that keep, and between the thresholds the markup drifts to rest, which is what brings a ratcheted markup down once the stockouts stop. Both fractions `[assumed]`; measured on the lone city: basket 96.9 before the shelf cap, 110.7 with the cap and the old thresholds, 103.9 with the shelf-aware thresholds.

assumed.subject: A merchant pays no more for an import than the going rate at home, marked up
assumed.summary: When the Armington split finds no domestic seller with stock, the buyer's landed-cost ceiling is the city's going wholesale rate for the good — the median asking price of its producers, with or without stock, times the wholesale markup tolerance — and quote × 1.2 only where the city makes none of the good (the island's grain).
assumed.body:
**When the Armington split finds no domestic seller with stock, the buyer's landed-cost ceiling is the city's going wholesale rate for the good — the median asking price of its producers, with or without stock, times the wholesale markup tolerance — and `quote × 1.2` only where the city makes none of the good (the island's grain).**
**Found:** the ceiling was `quote × 1.2` against any price at all, so Halvik's grocers, whose bakeries were sold out at that moment, imported bread from Dorsk at $19–22 a loaf against a domestic $5 and priced the shelf accordingly (the median grocer's loaf went 7.26 → 14.56 in a day).
**Over:** the last unit cost the buyer paid — it blends toward the very imports it should refuse.
**Because:** a grocer that pays four times its own selling price is not a merchant.
**Reversal cost:** cheap — one expression in `city/src/sim/systems/logistics.ts`; it may move the lone-city pin only if a lone city ever had a quote, which it does not.

assumed.subject: The buyer-collects cut of the haulage market — five routine choices
assumed.summary: From tuesday22's plan, 2026-09-08, on the principal's "haulage is a market" decision.
assumed.body:
From tuesday22's plan, 2026-09-08, on the principal's "haulage is a market" decision. Taken by the coordinator, not put to the principal, because each is routine. Tagged for confirmation.
**(a) A released lot is fetched by the buyer's own idle lorry first, else the yard's trucks, else any idle lorry in the city, hired** — reusing the existing `'toSeller'` vehicle state, a dead Phase 5 branch, so no new snapshot field.
**(b) A collecting lorry does not queue at the yard's gate this cut** — a hundred lorries single-file at one gate would be worse than two yard trucks; "how many bays" is its own decision.
**(c) Haulage is free this cut** — the city's fee comes when its number has a source.
**(d) A firm's one lorry serves its wholesale run, its export leg and its collections in that order of first refusal within a tick,** and a bumped export waits a tick in `pendingExports` rather than being lost.
**(e) An idle lorry that ended its run at its own depot has `pos` nulled** like every other returning lorry — `pos === null` is the sim's word for "indoors", a hashed field decided once.
**The planner's finding behind (a):** only farms, mills and bakeries own a lorry (`trucks: 1`); grocers, stalls, cafés and restaurants own none, so the buyer's-own-lorry option alone reaches wheat→mill and flour→bakery lots — which is why (a) adds hiring any idle lorry in the city, the market the principal asked for.
**Reversal cost:** cheap for all five.
**Depends on:** "Haulage out of the customs yard is a market, and the city takes a fee" (2026-09-08), which stays open on the shape of the market and the size of the fee.

assumed.subject: A lot leaves bond when the buyer takes it in, not when a lorry sets out
assumed.summary: CustomsLot.inTransit counts the units out on a lorry; the release loop hands out qty − inTransit; the door subtracts what it took, and what it had no room for is the lot's again, fetched when there is room.
assumed.body:
**`CustomsLot.inTransit` counts the units out on a lorry; the release loop hands out `qty − inTransit`; the door subtracts what it took, and what it had no room for is the lot's again, fetched when there is room.**
**Found by jarvis11:** `unloadImportRelease` destroyed the overflow when the buyer's store was full (`taken < loaded`, no return path), while the wholesale door has always carried its overflow home; the haulage market made two loads at one door likely (a 900-unit lot on the buyer's lorry and the yard's truck on successive ticks). A remainder under one unit is written off at the door and logged — no lorry loads a fraction. Snapshot version 7 → 8 (a new hashed field on every lot).
**Over:** returning the overflow to the shed's own shelf (stranded there, nobody sells it); sizing the load by the buyer's room at dispatch (room changes before arrival).
**Because:** no unit of a released import may vanish between the yard and the shelf; goods must be conserved like money, and nothing asserted it — a goods-conservation invariant for the validate suite is recorded as owed.
**Reversal cost:** cheap — one field, two lines each side.

assumed.subject: The cover a seller keeps back from the world counts its own customers' sales, not its exports
assumed.summary: Firm gains exportedToday/exported7d — booked at export loading, rolled at midnight beside sold7d — and the surplus cover is (sold7d − exported7d) / 7 × COVER_DAYS; the price rule and the backstop still read sold7d whole, as decided.
assumed.body:
**`Firm` gains `exportedToday`/`exported7d` — booked at export loading, rolled at midnight beside `sold7d` — and the surplus cover is `(sold7d − exported7d) / 7 × COVER_DAYS`; the price rule and the backstop still read `sold7d` whole, as decided.**
**Found:** the principal's words on 2026-09-08 were "the days of sales it keeps for its own customers"; the first implementation used `sold7d`, which since the same day's "every unit that leaves a firm's shelf is a sale" includes export loads — so a heavy exporter kept `4 × (exports + domestic)` back, and jarvis11 named the feedback (R6): exports raise the cover, the cover cuts the offer, the offer cuts exports, the counter decays, exports resume — a damped oscillator through a seven-day counter. The thirty-day diagnostic showed it: Halvik's farms sent the island 8,000 units of wheat in days 9–14, then offered nothing for two weeks while their counter carried those exports as "sales", and the island's mills starved.
**Over:** leaving the oscillation (recorded as "watch" that morning).
**Because:** an export is not the seller's own customer, and the principal's sentence said customers.
**Reversal cost:** cheap — two arrays on the firm, one subtraction; the lone-city pin does not move (a lone city exports nothing, and the arrays are zero) unless the snapshot's canonical form changes shape — say so if it does.
**Depends on:** "A firm offers the world only its surplus" and "Every unit that leaves a firm's shelf is a sale" (both 2026-09-08).
Argued in `city/DESIGN_NOTES_V2.md` §7 "Phase 4 — seven rules under the surplus rule, and three cities in band", the bullet "three smaller ones from the same read", where the oscillation was left open with numbers.

assumed.subject: The second sea lane — eleven routine choices
assumed.summary: From tuesday22's plan, 2026-09-08.
assumed.body:
From tuesday22's plan, 2026-09-08. Taken by the coordinator on the planner's recommendation, not put to the principal, because each is routine. Tagged for confirmation.
**(B) Dorsk's port sits on its existing coast** — every seed's map has a sea edge and a harbour district, so `port: true` needs no map change; to be confirmed on seed 42 / dorsk before any pin moves.
**(C) Dorsk gets the city-side quay** (a berth and a bonded warehouse), not a world-side-only port — `trade.ts` would otherwise record a sea arrival as a road lot in the land yard and tell the observatory a lie.
**(D) A city is a port because `PORT_CITIES` names it,** not because a built lane touches it — the alternative makes a city's map depend on who else is in the federation.
**(E) The new line shares `ship_knots`, `ship_capacity_units`, `max_wait_hours` and `ships_on_lane` with the first** — same class of ship, same line rule — and the two `why`s are amended to say "per line"; only the distance is authored per lane.
**(F) The distance is 880 nm,** derived from the 3D map's `[assumed]` `CITY_LAYOUT` (Dorsk sits 0.797 of Halvik's distance from the island; 1,100 × 0.80), so the lane a spectator sees and the lane the engine sails are one lane before Phase 8 reconciles them — at 14.5 knots a 61-hour passage, shorter than Halvik's 76, which is the point.
**(G) Two vessels on the line** — a 150-hour round trip halved is a 75-hour headway; one ship would leave the island's nearer supplier silent three days in four.
**(H) The freight market quotes per lane-direction as it already does** — no change.
**(I) The line is domiciled in Amaranth City** by the existing rule (the Isles are the shipping domicile, the point of the free port).
**(J) The FX-at-booking change lands before the lane, in its own commit,** because a price comparison between an NHK offer and a VYL offer is read off the rate.
**(K) The 3D camera frames the selected vessel's lane,** falling back to the first.
**Reversal cost:** cheap for all except (F), which is a number with a written derivation rather than a dataset — recorded so it can be argued.
**Depends on:** "A second sea lane, Dorsk ↔ Amaranth City" (2026-09-08).

assumed.subject: A surplus dumped abroad is an export, not a customer, and a firm's draw of an input is sized to what its own customers buy
assumed.summary: exportSurplus books exportedToday beside soldToday, and dailyDraw reads sold7d − exported7d for both the good itself and the output it makes — the same subtraction the seller's cover already makes.
assumed.body:
**`exportSurplus` books `exportedToday` beside `soldToday`, and `dailyDraw` reads `sold7d − exported7d` for both the good itself and the output it makes — the same subtraction the seller's cover already makes.** Taken by the coordinator on 2026-09-08 from tuesday22's finding, before the decision above and independent of it.
**Found:** without it a mill's wheat appetite read its own dumped flour as demand, and its reorder point outran its store — 11,700 kg against a 6,000 kg store by day 21, drawing 2,938 kg a day and climbing.
**Moves the lone-city pin** (`923adf3bb75b62f1` → `bb54cd9b4e4ba1d4`; basket 98.2 before and after). Validate's stock-days now read the engine's own `dailyDraw`, exported for the reading, instead of a copy that had already drifted.
**Reversal cost:** cheap.
**Depends on:** "[assumed] The cover a seller keeps back from the world counts its own customers' sales, not its exports" (2026-09-08) — the same subtraction, applied to the draw.

**Amendment (2026-09-08, after jarvis11):** the first cut netted `exported7d` — every export — out of the draw, which was right for a lone city (its only export is the dump) and wrong for a federated mill whose exports are real partner orders bounded by a partner's want. `Firm` now carries `dumpedToday`/`dumped7d`, written only by `exportSurplus`; the draw nets the dump; the seller's cover still nets every export, as decided. Snapshot 10 → 11; the lone-city pin `745f34cacccdb869` → `06173ff0eeec4458` for the shape alone.

assumed.subject: A repositioning leg is a sailing and an empty one, and moves no freight rate
assumed.summary: Under "A line sails to demand", a vessel that leaves empty to meet demand across is tagged Voyage.toDemand; it counts in the sailings and in the empty count (the decision's stated cost, kept honest) but does not push the freight index's load-factor rule.
assumed.body:
**Under "A line sails to demand", a vessel that leaves empty to meet demand across is tagged `Voyage.toDemand`; it counts in the sailings and in the empty count (the decision's stated cost, kept honest) but does not push the freight index's load-factor rule.** Taken by the coordinator on 2026-09-08 from jarvis11's lane S.
**Found:** the light direction was reaching the rate floor twice as fast for a policy reason, not a demand fact, and the same imbalance was already priced once as the loaded direction's low load factor.
**Also:** `nextSailing` publishes the hour an empty hull with demand across will actually leave, not its bound, so the "next departure" tile is not a promise the world breaks.
**Over:** recording every departure as a reading (as before).
**Reversal cost:** cheap — one boolean on a voyage, one argument to `recordSailing`.
**Depends on:** "A line sails to demand" (2026-09-08).

assumed.subject: The boundary inventory's share is read against the founding private weekly payroll
assumed.summary: Lane B2's economy.boundary row reports the foreign bill as a share of the founding private weekly payroll — a fixed yardstick set when the city is founded — not of the live wage bill.
assumed.body:
**Lane B2's `economy.boundary` row reports the foreign bill as a share of the founding private weekly payroll — a fixed yardstick set when the city is founded — not of the live wage bill.** Taken by the coordinator on 2026-09-09.
**Because:** a fixed denominator reads the same across days and seeds; a live one moves with the thing it measures.
**Reversal cost:** cheap — one denominator in validate.
**Revisit if a city grows:** a fixed yardstick understates the share of a payroll that has outgrown its founding.
**Depends on:** the service-bill entry (2026-09-08), whose first step this row was.

assumed.subject: Founding to customers — four routine choices
assumed.summary: From tuesday22's plan, 2026-09-09.
assumed.body:
From tuesday22's plan, 2026-09-09. Taken by the coordinator on the planner's recommendation, not put to the principal. Tagged for confirmation.
**(A) The border depot and the bonded warehouse are paid per lot from the customs account** — a real customer already in the world — rather than founded to nobody.
**(B) The warehouse is not founded** — no storage buyer exists — under "Kinds with no buyer are not founded until one exists" (2026-09-09).
**(C) The office's customer is the firms' services share of their wage bill plus the households' services divisions no other kind draws** — the two payments of "The engine pays what the calibration names" (2026-09-09), routed to the office.
**(D) Number fallbacks land as `param()` values with a `why` naming the loader that will replace them** (`city/worldkit/worldkit/loaders/{icio,ilostat,firms,consumption}.py`).
**Reversal cost:** cheap for all — (A) one payer, (B) one vacant premise, (C) two routings, (D) the badge the worldkit already uses.
**Depends on:** "Firms are founded to their customers" and the four `[confirmed]` entries above (all 2026-09-09).

**Amendment (2026-09-09, after jarvis11's read): (A) is superseded the same day.** As built, the border depot and the bonded warehouse were paid per present hour — not per lot — from an account that holds only fees (the FTA's tariffs are zero on every HS group), with the treasury behind it and bounded only by its balance. jarvis11 read that form for what it is: a treasury public-works customer no law names — the option the principal rejected under "The idle share is not the concern; the laws are" (2026-09-09). The sheds are **civic** now: the border's own infrastructure, in the treasury's sized budget, paid in the civic branch like the customs yard and the berth — one of each a city, as the founding already had them (Q1 of "Living World Phase 4, the principal's nine answers", 2026-09-05; (C) of "The second sea lane — eleven routine choices", 2026-09-08). Reversal cost: cheap — one branch in the sizing; the pins moved with the lane. Recorded because a payer "already in the world" that turns out to be the treasury under another name is the drift this log exists to catch. **Confirmed by the principal, 2026-09-09** — "[confirmed] The border sheds are civic", below.

assumed.subject: Founding to customers, landed — five choices made while measuring
assumed.summary: Taken by the coordinator on 2026-09-09 while landing the three lanes, each measured before it was kept; not put to the principal.
assumed.body:
Taken by the coordinator on 2026-09-09 while landing the three lanes, each measured before it was kept; not put to the principal. Tagged for confirmation.
**(a) One base for the bills and the sizing.** Lane P found the household bills applied the raw COICOP shares — shares of *total* consumption, in which food and housing already sit — to income after rent and food, a double subtraction that under-billed every shop 1.7× on Nordholm's numbers, while the sizing priced the same shops at gross income. Now the bills renormalise each division's share over `1 − share_food − share_housing`, and the sizing prices the bill-paid kinds at wages × (1 − savings rate − rent-to-income target − food share at the median) ÷ that rest — wages alone, not the dole or a pension: a household on either clears neither rent nor food at these rents and pays no bills (lane P counted 309 households of 974 with anything left on the first Friday).
**(b) The sizing's income is a fixed point of its own founding.** Priced at the calibrated 1,000 employed, the shops were founded to an income a town 36–44 % idle did not have, and earned half their wages. Now round 0 reads the calibrated employment at the mean wage and every round after reads the wage bill the previous round founded, offices and civic included, so the founding is priced at the customers it leaves in work. **Anchored, not fed back:** the treasury's civic budget and the sector caps stay at the calibrated level, because rents are per dwelling and do not follow the founding (tuesday22's trial paid every dole at 70 % idle from rent); a first cut that fed the founding into the civic payroll collapsed the town to 36 jobs. Result, seed 42: lone Halvik 386 of 2,442 slots (145 private, 241 civic), idle 61 %; federated Halvik 426 (167 + 259), 57 %; Dorsk 401 (160 + 241), 55 %; Amaranth City 458 (199 + 259), 63 %. One office per city (44–49 desks), from eighteen. **Confirmed by the principal, 2026-09-09** — the anchor was put as a question the same evening; "[confirmed] The fiscal anchor: the city's payroll is held at the calibrated level", below.
**(c) A farm floor founds premises, not slots.** The floor of two wheat farms had founded all sixteen of their slots when the mouths needed two; two whole farms earned a seventh of their wages. Now the floor is the least premises the payable slots are spread over — two farms of two slots each for 3,000 mouths.
**(d) The market stall is founded to nobody until it has a shelf.** Measured: stalls sold nothing in thirty days in any of the three cities, before and after the sizing. Founded "to households" who never come is the same fiction as the foreign bill.
**(e) The seven-day roll's warm-up is corrected in the view, not the engine.** The observatory's foreign-bill rate divides the roll by `7 × (1 − (6/7)^days)`, exact for a constant series; and two dashboard labels were renamed to fit two lines (`out of work`, `goods exported`) — seen in a browser.
**Measured after the fixed point (thirty federated days, revenue ÷ wages):** the food chain near one (grocer 1.4, bakery 0.8–1.2, mill 1.1–1.8); the office, clothing shop and hardware store about 0.5 on the mainland and about 1.0–1.2 on the island; the pharmacy 2.8–6.4, paid twice — the outing's cover and the health bill; farms 0.4–0.6 — the ×2 cover multiplier founds capacity that stands full half the time and pays wages for it; bars 7–14; the wider world drew nothing anywhere; baskets over twenty days Halvik 92.1–120.9, Dorsk 92.3–101.3, Amaranth City 91.7–106.9, all PASS; money conserved in all three currencies.
**Reversal cost:** cheap for (a), (c), (d), (e) — a formula, a floor, one vacant premise, a divisor in the view; moderate for (b) — the fixed point is the sizing's shape, and what it anchors (the civic budget, the sector caps) is a choice the principal has not seen — seen and confirmed the same evening, below; **every pin moves** with the lane, as its decision said.
**Depends on:** "Firms are founded to their customers", "The engine pays what the calibration names", "The idle share is not the concern; the laws are", "The farmland reduction folds into this lane", and "[assumed] Founding to customers — four routine choices" (all 2026-09-09).
**[friday22 note — resolved 2026-09-09]** (b) is a shape, not a number, and was put to the principal the same evening as the standing instruction requires; confirmed — "[confirmed] The fiscal anchor: the city's payroll is held at the calibrated level", below. Open item (i) still stands, and the two halves of (vi) the anchor did not settle — may the treasury borrow; do rents follow the town's income — are the principal's.

assumed.subject: Founding to customers, landed — after jarvis11's read
assumed.summary: Taken by the coordinator on 2026-09-09 after jarvis11 read the landed lanes, each measured before it was kept; not put to the principal.
assumed.body:
Taken by the coordinator on 2026-09-09 after jarvis11 read the landed lanes, each measured before it was kept; not put to the principal. Tagged for confirmation. The amendment to (A) of "four routine choices" (above) is from the same read.
**(a) The sizing prices the bill-paid kinds net of income tax at the cap.** The bills are paid from income after the tax the founding solves for, and the same gross cents were already the treasury's on the civic row. Fail-closed: it under-founds slightly.
**(b) A restore refuses a snapshot whose founding record disagrees with its firms, or whose residents hold jobs outside every founded firm's slots.** The record and the firms are two hashed authorities; a society that rewrites the record (the principal's land condition) must not restore against stale firms. **Confirmed by the principal, 2026-09-09** — refuse, not repair; "[confirmed] A restore refuses a snapshot whose founding record disagrees with its firms", below.
**(c) A founding that stops at the round cap is written `converged: false` with its `rounds`,** and the record's sentences are always the table priced at the founding as it stands.
**(d) The bills tally keeps no lifetime totals.** An index is not state; a reading that survives a restore differently is state in disguise.
**(e) Spotlights are appointed among adults only.** Once the founding changed who came first, creation order appointed a child, a working teen and an 84-year-old, and none was asked anything in two days.
**(f) The decisions feed test accounts for rows the ring dropped, and says so.** Founded to its customers, a 300-resident test town has one bar, and 148 evenings there in one 17:30 frame overrun the ring — (vii) below.
**(g) Validate's rent-to-income is read over renting households with an earner** — the calibration's own universe for the target — and the welfare-only households are printed beside it, not judged.
**(h) Two checks the founded town fails on the seven-day window are pinned in the tests with their reason, not widened.** Engel's quintile order — the bottom quintiles are dole households; the correlation stays negative and the check passes over thirty days. Rent-to-income — ~50–55 % over earners: rents were priced for a household with the calibrated number of earners and the founding leaves ~0.6. Likewise 63 % of commutes under an hour where the brief's town read 90 % — the jobs are where the customers are. Printed, not sized away, as the principal directed on the idle share ("dont woryy about this now … just make sure of the laws" — "The idle share is not the concern; the laws are", 2026-09-09).
**Measured (thirty federated days, seed 42, after every fix):** Halvik 399 of 2,382 slots founded (110 private, 289 civic), Dorsk 412 of 2,434, Amaranth City 434 of 2,418; lone Halvik 363 of 2,442 (41 firms in 141 premises, 100 vacant); idle 54–65 %; one office a city, from eighteen. The wider world moved 0.00 a day in every federated city and the boundary row reads `gated off`. Every check PASS except rent-to-income (49.5 % over 232 earning households in the lone city); Engel PASS over thirty days. Lone basket 95.5–115.3, ending 97.6; VYL ×0.747–×1.000, ending ×0.805; AMD pegged the whole month with 1.21 of 3 months of cover left; 73 shipments delivered, 0 short, 24 sailings; money conserved in all three currencies; the fake-minds recording re-recorded (97 answers); 598 tests.
**Reversal cost:** cheap for (a), (c), (d), (e), (f), (g) — a term, a flag, a tally, a filter, an account, a filter; moderate for (b) — a restore that refuses is a rule about what a snapshot is, and a society rewriting the record meets it first; (h) is a debt, not a cost — the two checks pass when the laws in (v) and (vi) below exist, and the pins say so.
**Depends on:** "[assumed] Founding to customers, landed — five choices made while measuring" (2026-09-09), whose (a) the tax term here refines and whose anchor (b) stands, now named as a law in (vi) below; "The idle share is not the concern; the laws are" and "Firms are founded to their customers" (both 2026-09-09).
**[friday22 note]** (h) pins two failing checks as expected failures. That is honest only while the log names the law that would make them pass — (v) and (vi) below, the principal's. If a third check joins them without a law named, the pin has become a way of not looking.

assumed.subject: Exit and entry, landed — after jarvis11's read
assumed.summary: Taken by the coordinator on 2026-09-09 after jarvis11 read the landed exit-and-entry lane; each item measured or verified before it was kept; not put to the principal.
assumed.body:
Taken by the coordinator on 2026-09-09 after jarvis11 read the landed exit-and-entry lane; each item measured or verified before it was kept; not put to the principal. Tagged for confirmation. The amendment to "Any agent may found in a vacant premise, with four weeks of wages" (above) is from the same read and is the one item of it that is not routine.
**(a) The closing law refuses a department at its own door.** `closeFirm` throws for a civic kind rather than relying on its one caller's guard — closing a school is the single irreversible act in the engine (nothing may found a civic kind again) and the function is meant to be called by an agent one day, not only by the loop that has the guard today.
**(b) A restore refuses a founding record that founds a premise no open firm stands in.** The firms-to-record check cannot see that shape, and a resident placed in those slots would work for ever unpaid. Asserted at restore only, because the founding law resizes a premise before it makes the firm that will stand in it — mid-founding, the disagreement is the law working.
**(c) The founding does its one throwing step — the resize — before a cent moves,** so a founding that fails charges nobody and leaves the record as it found it.
**(d) The closing threshold is read off the city's calibration bundle, not through `param()` with its own literal.** One law, one authority for its number; a country with no file borrows Nordholm's and says so.
**(e) A load a closed buyer refuses is written off and said when the seller has closed too,** rather than landing in a bin no loop reads.
**(f) The tests that assert what the treasury collects use the engine's own identity** — rent plus what was owed, less what is still owed — rather than a prediction from balances read a tick before the collection. Money moves in the tick the rent is taken, and the prediction was short by 14.87 NHK.
**Measured, ninety days, seed 42, after every fix:** lone Halvik's two grocers close on day 48 and a bakery on day 83, leaving ten workers seeking and the town with no grocer; Dorsk loses a wheat farm on day 69, its mill and a dairy on day 76, a second wheat farm on day 83 and a vegetable farm on day 90; Amaranth City a cafe on day 55, a grocer and a restaurant on day 62, a dairy on day 69 and a bar on day 83. Nothing re-founds any of them: the city founds nothing after day zero and no agent holds a policy yet. The treasury paid every wage and every dole in full throughout, drifting from NHK 7.9m to 4.8m. At sixty days ten of a hundred and four vacant premises have a customer the law can name. Pins: lone `4873830dae251aa9` unmoved; two-city `f65c078efbf46f4f` → `7639d4888ee161c8`, three-city `f101351e1f8a05bf` → `fe373191d9abb9ca`, both because those cities open with free civic slots that idle adults now take from the first morning.
**Reversal cost:** cheap for each — a guard, an assertion, an ordering, a lookup, a branch, a test identity. (a) and (b) are refusals rather than repairs, in the shape "A restore refuses a snapshot whose founding record disagrees with its firms" (2026-09-09) already set; reversing either means choosing to carry on past a state the law says cannot exist.
**Depends on:** "A firm closes after four short paydays", "Any agent may found in a vacant premise, with four weeks of wages", "A closing firm pays final wages first; the rest goes to the treasury", "Anyone without a job looks for one once a day", "Rents move two percent a month, a badged number", "The rent rise reads the whole city, and a household two months in arrears moves", "Civic is a department: the closing law does not reach the city's own firms" (all 2026-09-09) — the lane these land in; "A restore refuses a snapshot whose founding record disagrees with its firms" (2026-09-09) — (b) extends its check; "The treasury keeps a hard budget: no borrowing, no money created" (2026-09-09) — (f) reads the row it prints.
**[friday22 note]** The ninety-day reading is not a fault report, it is the argument for the next lane, and it belongs to the principal: eleven firms close across three cities in three months, nothing re-founds one, and the towns hollow out because the only entity that could found is a live agent policy that does not exist yet. Recorded as (xiii) of the Open note above. The treasury paying every wage in full while the private town empties is the second half of that reading — the hard budget is not what is failing.

assumed.subject: The founder of last resort, built — five choices, two badged numbers, and what it measured
assumed.summary: Taken by the coordinator on 2026-09-10 while building "The server is the government of the city, and it intervenes under law" (2026-09-09) to the coordinator's own reading of it — the city is the founder of last resort.
assumed.body:
Taken by the coordinator on 2026-09-10 while building "The server is the government of the city, and it intervenes under law" (2026-09-09) to the coordinator's own reading of it — the city is the founder of last resort. Each item was measured before it was kept; none was put to the principal. Tagged for confirmation.

**The rule as built, in one sentence.** At 00:00, after the exit law has run, the city walks its **vacant premises in building order** and founds **the first** one where all four hold: `canFound` names a customer who pays (the same `entryAnswer` an agent's founding is asked, so the city never founds a civic kind or a kind with no buyer); the premise has stood vacant at least **`assumptions/founding_<country>/last_resort_days` = 14**, counted from the tick it last emptied or from tick 0 for a premise the founder never filled; the treasury can put up the opening capital and still hold the week it owes; and the city has founded fewer than **`assumptions/founding_<country>/last_resort_per_week` = 1** firms in the last seven days. It pays **no fee to itself**. The firm is an ordinary firm under every law, the closing one included. Both numbers are badged `assumed` with a band and a `why` in `calibration/assumptions/founding_<country>.yaml`, written by the loader, rewritable by a society — the same badge the other three numbers of this lane wear.

**(a) The law runs in the same 00:00 tick as the exit law, straight after it, and before the daily seek.** The window, not the tick order, is what gives an agent first refusal: a premise that emptied at *this* midnight is on the walk and passed over, its vacancy being zero days old. What the placement buys is the other end — a firm the city founds at midnight has its slots in that morning's seek, so the town is not a day short of a grocer the city has already decided to open. Waiting a day would buy nothing the fourteen-day window does not already buy, and would cost the seek. `economy.lastResort` is a system of its own in `scheduler.ts`, between `economy.exit` and `economy.seek`.

**(b) The guard on the hard budget: the city founds only out of what stands above the week it owes.** `weekOwed` is a full week of the civic payroll at the founded slots' wages, at the upkeep the city pays over them, plus a week of pensions and dole at the standing rates for everyone out of work this minute; the city founds when `balance − capital ≥ weekOwed` and otherwise does not. Deliberately a *forward* commitment and not last week's outturn: the payday tally is a per-world reading that is never snapshotted (`labour.ts`), so a law that read it would answer differently after a restore, and every term of `weekOwed` is in the hash. One week and not four, because the hard budget already pays part wages and part dole when it is short and says so — the reserve exists to stop a founding *causing* that, not to make the treasury solvent for a quarter.

One test moved with (a) and is worth naming, because it is the law's shape showing up in an old assertion: `tests/exit.test.ts` checked that a closing adds exactly the remainder plus the final tax to the treasury in that tick. It no longer does — the city founds in the same tick, out of the same treasury — so the assertion now subtracts the opening money the city put up at that midnight. The exit law's own arithmetic is unchanged; what changed is that midnight has two laws in it.

**(c) The walk stops at the first premise it cannot pay for.** The city does not skip an expensive premise to found a cheap one further down the street; that is the state choosing ventures, the shape the principal rejected. Building order, and it stops — one line a day in the city log when it does. A refusal on the window or on the customer is not said at all: that is the ordinary state of a hundred vacant premises, and a line a day for each is not a log.

**(d) The city is written on the record as `founder: null`, not as an invented principal id.** The city holds no account in `world.agents.principals`, writes no mandate and takes no decision on the chain, so an id would point at nothing. `null` is the engine's own word for "no principal", and on `FoundingRecord.foundings` — where every row *is* a founding after day zero — it can mean only one thing. `foundedByCity()` is the reader; `Firm.founder` stays null too. The inspector's sentence reads **"founded on day 62 by the city with 2 slots"** where an agent's reads a resident's name.

**(e) A city founding is not written to the agent audit chain.** The chain records what agents did under mandates; the city holds none, and a row asserting an agent acted would have no fact behind it — jarvis11's standing reading of the founding gate (2026-09-09), applied. The founding record and the city log carry it.

**Reported, never judged.** `bench/validate.ts`'s treasury row gains three columns — firms the **city** founded, firms an **agent** founded, and the opening money the city put up — so the day agents outfound the city is visible, which is the number friday22 named as the one to watch. `checks.length` stays 6; no check reads any of the three.

**Measured, seed 42, a hundred and twenty days, after every fix.** *Lone Halvik:* both grocers close on day 48; the city founds a grocer the same midnight (8 slots, NHK 324.69 of opening money) and a second on day 55 (2 slots, NHK 80.05); those two close on days 90 and 104 and the city founds again in the premises the first pair left. Day 120: 39 firms open, **two grocers**, four closings, four city foundings, NHK 809.48 of capital put up, treasury NHK 7.91m → 4.10m, every civic wage and every dole paid in full on every sampled day. Before this law the same town ended with no grocer. *Federated:* Halvik 14 closings and 10 city foundings (NHK 3,681.44 of capital), Dorsk 13 and 11 (VYL 1,060.99), Amaranth City 8 and 9 (AMD 2,495.59); Halvik ends with one grocer (its second closed on day 118, inside its window), Dorsk two, Amaranth City three. Treasuries: Halvik NHK 8.35m → 4.28m, Dorsk VYL 3.20m → 1.01m, Amaranth City AMD 9.72m → 1.29m — the city's foundings are 3–9 % of each fall, so **the founder of last resort is not what drains the treasury**; the civic payroll against rent and tax is, as it was before this law. **Agent-founded: 0 in every city, as expected — no agent holds a founding policy until Phase 6.** The three pinned hashes are unmoved (lone `4873830dae251aa9`, two-city `7639d4888ee161c8`, three-city `fe373191d9abb9ca`): the law's first act is on day 48 and the pinned windows end on days 7 and 14.

**The thing this law does not do, and the reason to re-open it at Phase 6.** The window counts a **premise's vacancy**, not the **age of the opportunity**. So the first city founding lands on the *same midnight* as the closing that freed the customer — day 48 in every city measured — because the premise it takes has stood vacant since day zero and has long served its fourteen days; the window bites only on a premise that emptied recently. Under the law as written that is correct: nobody founded in that premise for forty-seven days. But an agent policy would have had no reason to found there before the customer existed, and "first refusal" means less than the number 14 suggests. Counting from the tick `canFound` first said yes would mean per-premise state on the hashed record; it was not built, and this is the item to weigh when a Phase 6 policy exists and the city-against-agent count is read for the first time.

**Superseded later the same day (2026-09-10): "[confirmed] The agent looks first", below.** Measured in the lone city, this is worse than the paragraph above states: a vacant premise with a nameable customer exists on **7 days of 120**, so there is no fortnight in which an agent could act and the window buys an agent nothing at all; the **per-week cap** is the only thing holding the city back. The principal's answer is order, not a longer or better-counted window: the founding policy runs in the same midnight, immediately before this walk. The window and the cap both stay as built.

**Reversal cost:** cheap for both numbers — two `param()` values with a `why`, three countries, and the pins move whenever a number does. Moderate for the law: it is the second founding path in the engine, it writes the founding record the restore rule reads, and it changes what a vacant premise means — an opportunity on a clock rather than one waiting indefinitely. Reversing it after Phase 6 means towns kept whole by the city start hollowing again, with every pin moving.

**Depends on:** "The server is the government of the city, and it intervenes under law" (2026-09-09) — the direction and the reading this builds; "Any agent may found in a vacant premise, with four weeks of wages" and its fail-closed amendment (2026-09-09) — the same `canFound`, the same price, and the first refusal the window protects; "A firm closes after four short paydays" (2026-09-09) — the law the city's own firms are under; "The treasury keeps a hard budget: no borrowing, no money created" (2026-09-09) — (b); "The city earns from what it makes and serves; fees to agents are very small, or a reward" (2026-09-09) — no fee to itself; "Civic is a department: the closing law does not reach the city's own firms" (2026-09-09) — this founds no civic kind and does not widen that branch; "A restore refuses a snapshot whose founding record disagrees with its firms" (2026-09-09) — (d) writes the row it reads; "Idle hours are bought" (2026-09-09) — why the firms the city re-founds close again in their turn.

**[friday22 note]** Over a hundred and twenty days the city founded ten to eleven firms a city and agents founded none, which is exactly the shape the principal was warned of when this was recorded: until Phase 6 the last resort *is* the only resort, and every reading taken before then will look like the state as sole entrepreneur. The two things that keep it honest are in place and printed — the window and the one-a-week cap on one side, the city-against-agent count on the other. The churn is worth watching too: in the lone city the two firms the city founded on days 48 and 55 both closed within six weeks and were replaced, which is the closing law reading a customer the town cannot really pay for, not the founding law failing.
