assumed.subject: Ratings, built — and what jarvis11 corrected
assumed.summary: Chose: the third lane of the [assumed] build order, landed.
assumed.body:
**Chose:** the third lane of the `[assumed]` build order, landed. Everything below is the coordinator's shape for "[confirmed] Reputation: agents rate each other, as signed acts on the chain (rules 14/15)" (2026-09-12); the principal chose the law, not these mechanics.

**(a) The act — `rate(host, by, about, score, because, tick, signature)` in `city/src/agents/ratings.ts`.** A holder's signed act over `ratingBody(realm, by, about, score, because, tick)`, `tick` the world's own. The engine writes no opinion: a resident's principal cannot rate. `about` is a merchant — a firm's account by the ledger's kinds (`AgentHost.isMerchant`, `World.isMerchant`) — and not the wallet of any agent of the rater's, so a holder cannot rate its own firm. Anything else is refused and writes nothing.

**(b) The defences, as the law.** Only after a purchase: the rater's personal agent, active, bought from the merchant within the rolling day, read off `Agent.spent` (rule 8's log). Entries of category rent, founding, wage or refund are not purchases — **jarvis11's finding:** the first draft let a tenant rate its landlord off a rent payment and a founder rate the treasury. Once per rater per merchant per day. Score 1..5, whole. Words at most `BECAUSE_MAX_CHARS`, refused not clamped. **A departure from the `[confirmed]` entry, recorded as the honest reading:** that entry says "a chain row both were parties to"; the ring cannot be read for it and the ledger keeps no rows, so the spend log is the evidence of the transaction, not a chain row.

**(c) The record.** `AgentState.ratings` — hashed, append-only, absent until the first, never compacted; the one unbounded hashed array in the agent layer, said (amended 2026-09-12: one of two — `AgentState.disputes` is the other; see "[assumed] Disputes, built" (d) below). Each rating is a chain row `rating:firm:given` with `signedBy: 'holder'` and the words — the bounded-reason rule of 2026-09-08, extended to outside-authored text.

**(d) The reading — `reputationOf`.** The mean over ratings inside `RATING_LIFE` (90 days, `[assumed]`) whose rater stands on its record — agent active, household not in arrears — at weight 1, else weight 0 (`discounted`). `expired` ratings are kept and not read. `raters` (distinct) is the number the page says, not `counted` — one customer rating daily is one customer. `weighted` says whether the arrears weight was applied; a bare agent host cannot apply it. `[assumed]`: the weights and the life are the coordinator's numbers; the weight is read at reading time, not the rating's; the arrears weight reads household state that is not on the chain, so an outside reader can reproduce `raters` and the mean but not the discount.

**(e) The page.** The building panel prints "rated 4.3 by 3 customers over 7 ratings (1 discounted, 2 lapsed)". Reported, never judged.

**(f) Not built, said.** Residents cannot rate until they hold keys (Phase 7). Ratings of agents — service counterparties — wait on a service market. The engine's leftover `Agent.reputation` field is written at creation and read by nothing; kept because removing it moves every hash. A ring of holders rating each other's firms is bounded, not prevented.

**(g) Tests.** `city/tests/ratings.test.ts` (5). Pins unmoved.

**Over:** rating off any spend entry (jarvis11 — rent and founding are not purchases); clamping an over-long reason (refused instead, so the signed bytes are what is stored); a city-kept score (rejected by the principal).

**Because:** D-2 — a rating is an act a holder performs under a law, and the engine only records and reads it; D-3 — the act and the words are on the chain for anyone to verify.

**Reversal cost:** cheap for (d) and (e) — numbers and a reading. Moderate for (a)–(c) once a rating exists: chain rows and the hashed array are never deleted, so a changed law leaves rows every reading must learn to ignore.

**Depends on:** "[confirmed] Reputation: agents rate each other" (2026-09-12); "[assumed] Build order for the four laws" (2026-09-12); "[assumed] The kill switch, built" (2026-09-12) — the holder's key and the signed-act shape; "[confirmed] Every unit that leaves a firm's shelf is a sale" (2026-09-08) — what a purchase is; the 2026-09-08 bounded-reason rule; D-2; D-3.

**[friday22 note]** (b)'s spend-log evidence and (d)'s 90-day life, weights and reading-time discount are the two gaps the `[confirmed]` entry's note named, now filled by the coordinator — the principal has not seen the numbers. The discount reading off-chain state means the reputation the city shows and the reputation an outside reader can reproduce differ; that is a D-3 cost to put to the principal, not to leave standing.

assumed.subject: Disputes, built — and what jarvis11 corrected
assumed.summary: Chose: the fourth and last lane of the [assumed] build order, landed.
assumed.body:
**Chose:** the fourth and last lane of the `[assumed]` build order, landed. Everything below is the coordinator's shape for "[confirmed] A dispute is a signed claim citing chain rows; the engine publishes what the chain shows; the parties may name an arbiter (rule 16)" (2026-09-12); the principal chose the law, not these mechanics.

**(a) The claim — `raise(host, by, against, cited, claim, tick, signature)` in `city/src/agents/disputes.ts`.** A holder's signed claim over `disputeBody(realm, by, against, cited, claim, tick, seq)` — `tick` the world's own, `seq` the claimant's act sequence (`Agent.acts`) — so a claim is single-use. One claim per claimant per day (`[assumed]`, the ratings cadence). `against` is a principal, or a firm's account (by `isMerchant`). Cited rows: one to `CITED_MAX` (32, `[assumed]`), none twice, all already written. Refused, writing nothing: a claimant whose key is the world's or whose agent is not active; a claim against oneself or one's own firm; an unknown respondent; words over the bound; another tick; a bad signature.

**(b) The reading — `readCited`.** For each cited row still in the retained ring: subject, actor, cents, tick, whether the claimant's agent wrote it, and whether each party is on it — by one predicate for both sides (its agent is the actor, or an account it runs is the counterparty). **jarvis11's finding:** the first draft read the two sides by different predicates and could say a respondent was absent from a row it was on. For each cited row the ring has compacted: that it is gone, and `compactedThrough` at the reading. A finding of fact, never a judgement; no money moves. The chain row `dispute:raised` carries the cited seqs and which were seen and which gone — **jarvis11's second finding:** the first draft carried counts only, so an outside reader could not check the reading against the exported chain.

**(c) The arbiter.** `nameArbiter` — both parties sign `arbiterBody` for a third holder, neither party, whose agent is active. **jarvis11's third finding:** the first draft let a halted or banned holder be named and rule. A respondent whose key is the world's (a city firm, a resident's firm) cannot sign, so such a dispute stands on the reading alone (`respondentPrincipal` null). `rule` — the arbiter, still active, rules once (for-claimant / for-respondent / no-finding) with signed words; the chain row is `dispute:ruled`, `signedBy: 'arbiter'`. The engine enforces nothing from a ruling.

**(d) Hashed state.** `AgentState.disputes` — append-only, never compacted. The second unbounded hashed array in the agent layer (the ratings entry's (c) said "the one"; it is now one of two), and the one place chain rows are copied outside the ring — a reading keeps up to 32 rows. Bounded by one claim a day per claimant.

**(e) Not built, said.** Nothing reads a dispute yet — not the page, not validate, not the ratings law's reading; a reader is a later lane. Rule 16's liability tiers are not built: the engine moves no money on a dispute and the principal chose no fines. A claim may be raised against a principal who has left — the identity persists.

**(f) `[assumed]` numbers, for the principal.** 32 cited rows; one claim a day; "any active holder who is neither party" as arbiter; a ruling binds nothing.

**(g) Tests.** `city/tests/disputes.test.ts` (3). Pins unmoved. This completes the four-law build order — kill switch, leaving, ratings, disputes.

**Over:** one predicate per side (jarvis11 — a respondent could be read as absent from its own row); counts only on the chain row (jarvis11 — unverifiable by an outside reader); any holder as arbiter (jarvis11 — a halted or banned holder could rule); the city ruling or fining (rejected by the principal).

**Because:** D-2 — the claim, the naming and the ruling are acts holders perform under a law; the engine states what the chain holds and never judges. D-3 — the cited seqs and the seen/gone list on the chain row let anyone with the exported chain check the reading.

**Reversal cost:** cheap for (a), (c), (f) — doors and numbers. Moderate for (b) and (d) once a dispute exists: the copied rows and the hashed array are never deleted, and a changed reading leaves rows every later reader must learn to ignore. Expensive if a ruling is later made to move money — that is the city taking money on a judgement, which the principal did not choose.

**Depends on:** "[confirmed] A dispute is a signed claim citing chain rows…" (2026-09-12); "[assumed] Build order for the four laws" (2026-09-12); "[assumed] The kill switch, built" (2026-09-12) — `Agent.acts`, the single-use signature shape, "active"; "[assumed] Ratings, built" (2026-09-12) — the daily cadence, the hashed-array shape; "[assumed] Leaving and the return, built" (2026-09-12) — a departed principal is still an identity a claim can name; D-2; D-3.

**[friday22 note]** The `[confirmed]` entry's note left open who may be an arbiter and what a ruling binds; (c) and (f) fill both with the coordinator's answers — any active third holder, and nothing. The principal has not seen either. (d)'s copied rows are a second place the chain is held; if the ring's compaction and a reading's copy ever disagree, the reading is what the chain showed at that tick, not what it shows now — say so wherever a dispute is read.

assumed.subject: The firm's agent on the snapshot; disputes on a firm's page (commit 1e4cad2)
assumed.summary: Chose: two closures, the coordinator's, landed without asking.
assumed.body:
**Chose:** two closures, the coordinator's, landed without asking. `Firm.agent` is carried on the snapshot as an optional key, present only when set (a resident-founded firm), so a restored world keeps the tie from a firm to its operating agent without re-finding it; the day-zero town and the three pins encode as before, and `firmAgentOf` still re-finds the agent for a snapshot written before the key existed. The inspector's building panel lists the disputes about a firm beside its rating, off `disputesAbout` and printed by `disputesSentence` — how many raised, how many stand on the reading alone, how many ruled and which way — a reading, nothing judged. This is the reader the disputes entry's (e) said did not exist, for the page only; `validate` still has no row for disputes or ratings, since no `validate` run holds a holder.
**Over:** re-finding the firm's agent on every restore (fragile once two agents can be tied to one firm); a panel that scores or ranks disputes (the engine does not judge — rule 16 as confirmed).
**Because:** D-2 — the page shows what the chain and the state hold; D-3 — a restored world must answer as the live one did.
**Reversal cost:** cheap — an optional snapshot key and a panel sentence; the key's absence on old snapshots is already handled.
**Depends on:** "[assumed] Disputes, built" (2026-09-12); "[assumed] Phase 6 under D-2, the first three lanes landed" (2026-09-11) — the firm's agent.

assumed.subject: The port bench across the border (commit b400391)
assumed.summary: Chose: npm run port -- --federate (city/bench/port.ts) presents the same passport at every city of the federation.
assumed.body:
**Chose:** `npm run port -- --federate` (`city/bench/port.ts`) presents the same passport at every city of the federation. Each city admits it into its own money — Halvik, Dorsk and Amaranth City, one identity, three households, three credits in three currencies — and a mandate signed for Halvik's realm is refused at Dorsk and at Amaranth City, because the realm is in the signed body (`signedMandateBody(draft, id, realm)`); the bench prints the refusal reason from each door. It writes nothing to the repo and is the same run every time. **`[assumed]`, the coordinator's:** one identity may hold a household in several cities at once, and nothing links them — no shared credit, no shared reputation, no shared disputes across cities. The principal has not been asked whether one identity, several domiciles, is the federation's meaning or a hole in it.
**Over:** one household per identity across the federation (would need a federation-level register nothing owns yet); a mandate valid in any city (rejected on 2026-09-12 — a signature binds to its city).
**Because:** D-1 — domicile is per jurisdiction, and the bench is how the principal watches the port before an outside agent arrives; "a signature binds to its city" ("[assumed] jarvis11's read of the holder lane", 2026-09-12).
**Reversal cost:** cheap for the bench; moderate for the `[assumed]` — once identities hold in several cities, linking them later means deciding which credit was the second.
**Depends on:** "[confirmed] The passport carries the first mandate" (2026-09-12); "[confirmed] A returning identity is a return" (2026-09-12) — the credit is once per identity *per city* under this reading, which that decision did not say.
**[friday22 note]** "Once per identity, ever" (the returning-identity decision) and "a credit in each city" (this bench) are not the same sentence. The principal decided the first about one city; the second is the coordinator's extension to three. Put to him with (xxx) below.

assumed.subject: The holder's inbox: what waits on a signature (commit bf0ca3c)
assumed.summary: Chose: inboxOf(host, principal, tick) in city/src/agents/inbox.ts — a derivation, never state, and null for a principal whose key is in the world (a resident, a city firm).
assumed.body:
**Chose:** `inboxOf(host, principal, tick)` in `city/src/agents/inbox.ts` — a derivation, never state, and null for a principal whose key is in the world (a resident, a city firm). It lists: the holder's halted agents and under what; every pending escalation of its agents with what was asked, when it lapses, the grant draft a yes must carry and the register's next id to sign it under; the disputes the holder is party to and what each waits on (`'an arbiter'` | `'the ruling'`); the standing intent's expiry, so the next is signed before it lapses; and the act sequence to sign into a halt, a resume, a leaving or a claim. A server hands it to the holder or the holder polls it; a yes signed straight from it lands. The engine still decides nothing in a holder's name — it now says, in one place, what it is waiting for. **`[assumed]`, the coordinator's:** expired escalations are not shown (`tick >= expiresAt` is skipped) — they are already undecided by silence, and showing them would invite a signature the door would refuse.
**Over:** inbox as hashed state (a second copy of what the agents, escalations and disputes already hold — and one more thing a restore could disagree on); showing lapsed escalations greyed (nothing to sign; noise).
**Because:** friday22's note, twice ("[assumed] The holder signs" and "[assumed] jarvis11's read of the holder lane", 2026-09-12): an escalation expires by silence in three sim-hours and nothing announced that the agent was waiting. Silence is not a decision, and a holder cannot answer what it is not shown.
**Reversal cost:** cheap — a derivation over existing state; nothing hashed, nothing on the chain.
**Depends on:** "[assumed] The holder signs — lanes P1–P3" (2026-09-12); "[assumed] The kill switch, built" (2026-09-12) — `Agent.acts`; "[assumed] Disputes, built" (2026-09-12).

assumed.subject: The port bench reads the inbox (working tree, city/bench/port.ts)
assumed.summary: Chose: the bench ends by printing the holder's inbox (step 7b, after the return): agents halted, escalations pending, disputes waiting, whether an intent stands and when it lapses, the act sequence — and one line per waiting dispute.
assumed.body:
**Chose:** the bench ends by printing the holder's inbox (step 7b, after the return): agents halted, escalations pending, disputes waiting, whether an intent stands and when it lapses, the act sequence — and one line per waiting dispute. On seed 42 it shows one dispute, "as claimant, waits on an arbiter": the claim the bench raised against the grocer in step 4, which, the grocer being the city's, no one can sign an arbiter for. Nothing decided; the bench is the reading the principal watches, and this is the first time it shows what the port is still waiting on.
**Over:** nothing — a print.
**Because:** the inbox entry above says a server hands it to the holder; the bench is the holder's stand-in, so it should read it too.
**Reversal cost:** cheap.
**Depends on:** "[assumed] The holder's inbox" (2026-09-13).

assumed.subject: tuesday22's plan for the next lanes, adopted
assumed.summary: Chose: the coordinator adopted tuesday22's four lanes in order.
assumed.body:
**Chose:** the coordinator adopted tuesday22's four lanes in order. **A** — `validate --holders N`: seat N holders in a `validate` run so its report has a row for ratings, disputes and the inbox; reported, never judged. **B** — a door catalogue: one `present` dispatcher over every door an outside agent can knock on, with deterministic vectors so a conformance run is the same every time. **C** — the worker's `present` seam: the worker accepts a `present` while running and refuses `world-moved` while it does, so a door cannot land on a world that has stepped under it. **D** — residents holding keys, parked as the principal's question: whether a resident (key in the world) may become a holder, and by what act. A–C are the coordinator's mechanics under decisions already recorded; D is not started and not to be tagged `[assumed]` when it is.
**Over:** the page before validate (the page has its reader; validate has none); D first (a question, not a lane).
**Because:** D-3 — the launch gate is "verified by anyone with `curl` and the validator", and today neither validate nor a catalogue can show a holder's laws firing.
**Reversal cost:** cheap — an order of work.
**Depends on:** D-3; the four 2026-09-13 entries above.

assumed.subject: Lane A — validate --holders N: the port laws in the standard report, reported and never judged (commit 6d52c9c)
assumed.summary: Chose: the validate report carries a standing row for the port laws, and it is a row, not a check.
assumed.body:
**Chose:** the validate report carries a standing row for the port laws, and it is a row, not a check. N outside holders are admitted and walked through every door on a fixed timetable, and what each door said is tallied per city — admissions, mandates verified under the holder's key, ratings, disputes, halts, resumes, leavings, returns, the money the wider world holds at the end, and every refusal by door, by whom and reason. Nothing is judged and nothing is thrown: a rating presented before the agent has bought anything is refused by the ratings law and printed as the tell it is. jarvis11's read separated a refusal `by: 'law'` (the door spoke) from a deferral `by: 'bench'` (the bench had no honest row to cite yet), each its own column; the bench reads "a purchase" through the law's own `isPurchase` (exported from `ratings.ts`), not a copy. At `--holders 0`, the default, the report is byte-for-byte what it was, lone and federated — the row is absent, not empty. Seed 42, twelve days: Halvik admits 3 of 3, 4 of 4 signed mandates verify, 3 ratings, 3 disputes, one halt, one resume, one leaving, one return, nothing held abroad; hash `1d78a1317d9c95a1`, pins untouched. **`[assumed]`, the coordinator's, not put to the principal:** holders admitted at day 2 09:00; keys derived from `validate:<seed>:<i>` so the DIDs are the same on every run and at every city (the passport re-signed per city, since the city is in the signed body); the timetable — a rating the hour after the agent's first purchase, the dispute the day after, halt and resume on day 5, leaving day 6, return day 9 — designed off a probe (an agent's `spent` is pruned to the last day and the chain's ring turns over many times a day, so the purchase row is read the hour it appears or not at all); and the `by: 'law' | 'bench'` split of refusals.
**Over:** a check that passes or fails on the port laws (the engine does not judge — rule 16 as confirmed, and D-2); a rating on a calendar date rather than after the purchase (the row would be gone from the ring); a bench-side copy of what counts as a purchase (drifts from the law); a row present-but-empty at `--holders 0` (a run that never heard of the flag must not carry its shadow).
**Because:** D-3 — the gate is "verified by anyone with `curl` and the validator", and until this lane no run of `validate` had a holder in it; lane A of "[assumed] tuesday22's plan for the next lanes, adopted" (2026-09-13).
**Reversal cost:** cheap for the report row and the timetable (bench code, nothing hashed on the default path); moderate for the `validate:<seed>:<i>` keys if anyone comes to rely on those DIDs across runs — they are test identities and must never hold value.
**Depends on:** "[assumed] tuesday22's plan for the next lanes, adopted" (2026-09-13); "[assumed] The holder's inbox" (2026-09-13); "[assumed] The port bench across the border" (2026-09-13) — the per-city re-signed passport; "[assumed] Disputes, built" and "[assumed] The holder signs — lanes P1–P3" (both 2026-09-12). Standing beside it: (xxx) — the port bench's holder still sees one dispute waiting on an arbiter nobody can sign for.

assumed.subject: Lane B — the door catalogue: one caller into every seam (commit 051d5b8)
assumed.summary: Chose: present(world, act) in city/src/sim/systems/present.ts is the one switch over every door a holder can knock on.
assumed.body:
**Chose:** `present(world, act)` in `city/src/sim/systems/present.ts` is the one switch over every door a holder can knock on. `Act` is the tagged union — the passport with its opening mandate, a signed mandate, an escalation's answer with the grant a yes carries, the countersignature, the three halts, the leaving, the rating, the claim, the arbiter, the ruling — with the doors' own field names; `bodyOf(world, act)` returns the exact bytes each door verifies at the world's tick and realm. No act carries a tick or a realm as an argument: `world.tick` fills every tick slot and each door reads `realmOf` itself; the mandate drafts carry `issuedAt`/`expiresAt` inside the signed body and the passport carries `city`, and the doors check those against the world (jarvis11 corrected the first cut's claim that the union carried no tick at all; tested with a draft issued one minute ahead). It verifies nothing, writes nothing, adds no rule, and reports only the seqs the chain gained. The seq a leaving or a claim carries is read through the door's own reader (`leavingSeqOf`, `claimSeqOf`). `docs/DOORS.md` is the table: kind, door, body and argument order, the refusals in the door's own words, the vectors that cover it. **`[assumed]`, the coordinator's and jarvis11's, not put to the principal:** the catalogue lives in `sim/systems/`, not `agents/` — jarvis11's ruling that the first placement was a layer inversion (the one file in the agent layer importing the economy it is bound by, on an import cycle that held only by the order of `index.ts`), and that the seam that knows both sides belongs beside the other systems; `bench/doors-vectors.ts` writes `public/doors/vectors.json` — twenty-nine vectors on seed 42 over the port bench's world, one wrong-realm (or, for the realm-less delegation body, wrong-key) refusal per kind, the world hash at each, the subjects each landing wrote — byte-identical run to run, its key seeds public and its DIDs test identities that must never hold value; `tests/present.test.ts` rebuilds the world from the file's own description and replays it, the start hash the first line a stale file fails on; an unknown kind off the wire is refused `no such door`, the dispatcher's own sentence, not a crash.
**Over:** a server or replayer reaching twelve doors in five files with five argument orders one by one (gets one wrong); acts that carry their own tick or realm (a holder could present bytes for a minute or a city the world is not at); the catalogue in `agents/` (the inversion above); vectors generated fresh per run (a conformance run must be the same every time).
**Because:** D-3 — publishable conformance: an outside agent on any framework, verified by anyone with the validator, needs one documented entry and a fixed vector set; lane B of "[assumed] tuesday22's plan for the next lanes, adopted" (2026-09-13).
**Reversal cost:** cheap to move the file or rename kinds while nothing outside calls it; expensive once `public/doors/vectors.json` and `docs/DOORS.md` are what an outside framework conforms to — the vector file is a published contract from the day it is served.
**Depends on:** "[assumed] tuesday22's plan for the next lanes, adopted" (2026-09-13); every door it dispatches to — "[assumed] The holder signs — lanes P1–P3", "[assumed] P5 — the holder countersigns its agent's delegation", "[assumed] The kill switch, built", "[assumed] Disputes, built", "[assumed] Leaving and the return, built" (all 2026-09-12); "a signature binds to its city" ("[assumed] jarvis11's read of the holder lane", 2026-09-12).

assumed.subject: Lane C — the worker's present seam: a door onto a message port, fail-closed (commit 069be93)
assumed.summary: Chose: the worker's seam adds one rule and no door.
assumed.body:
**Chose:** the worker's seam adds one rule and no door. A holder's bytes carry the world's minute and the register's next id, and a world whose timer is running has already left that minute or will have before the door reads it, so the worker does not race the door: a `present` on a running world is refused `world-moved` with the tick, nothing written, and the panel pauses before it asks for the bytes. The worker signs nothing and infers nobody — a message on the port has no identity, the signature is the only thing that speaks for the holder, and the door verifies it under the key the world already holds; the key never enters the page, the panel hands out bytes and takes back a signed act. `present` is the catalogue's (lane B); the worker's own vocabulary is the refusal. **`[assumed]`, the coordinator's and jarvis11's, not put to the principal, and beyond the plan entry:** the refusal is two-sided — `world-moved` for a running world *and* `held` for a federated city stopped at the hour barrier, since its tick's instruction has not been applied and an act landing there would put the chain in an order no straight run reaches (the `held` half was added on jarvis11's F4 and is not in the plan entry above, which said `world-moved` only); no hold-with-timeout — the worker never pauses the world on a holder's behalf, the page pauses; reads (an inbox, a body) are derivations off state, answered whether or not the world runs and stamped with the tick they were read at, so bytes fetched from a moving world are visibly bytes for a minute that has passed; a door that throws after it has written drops the world, the way `drain`'s guard drops an interrupted tick — the worker cannot know the doors validate before writing, so it checks the chain count itself; every request is answered under its id even when a handler throws, and `terminate` rejects what waits rather than dropping it; and the inbox is readable by anyone who types a principal id — derivations only, the grant draft it shows is bytes, not authority, and nothing lands without the holder's signature.
**Over:** letting the door's own refusal answer a late act (right only by accident of timing); the worker holding the world for a holder with a timeout (a number nobody chose, and a holder's silence stalling a city); refusing reads while running (the inbox is a reading, and a holder must see what waits before it signs); a stuck promise on a throwing handler (a refusal nobody said); telling a `held` city's holder to pause (the world is not running — the sentence would be false).
**Because:** D-3 — an outside agent must reach the running city's door and be refused honestly rather than raced; "a stuck promise is a refusal nobody said" is the same rule as the chain's — silence is not a decision ("[assumed] The holder's inbox", 2026-09-13); lane C of "[assumed] tuesday22's plan for the next lanes, adopted" (2026-09-13).
**Reversal cost:** cheap for `world-moved`/`held` (a worker-side refusal; no door, no chain row); moderate for the open inbox — once a server exposes it, closing it to the principal's own key is a protocol change every client feels.
**Depends on:** "[assumed] Lane B — the door catalogue" (2026-09-13) — `present` is its; "[assumed] The holder's inbox" (2026-09-13); "[assumed] tuesday22's plan for the next lanes, adopted" (2026-09-13); the federation's hour barrier ("Phase 4 — the sea" lanes, 2026-09-10/11) for `held`. Federation-wide presents are deferred to the city port, not built — (xxxi).
**[friday22 note]** The plan entry above said the worker "accepts a `present` while running and refuses `world-moved` while it does"; what landed is refuses-while-running and answers only on a paused world. That is the stricter and honest reading, but it is not the sentence recorded, and the principal has not seen either. The open inbox — anyone may read what any principal is waiting for — is a privacy posture nobody asked him about; it is the kind of thing D-1's "laws are the attraction" turns on.

assumed.subject: Adoption, built — and what jarvis11 corrected (commit 117ad2d)
assumed.summary: Chose: lane D landed.
assumed.body:
**Chose:** lane D landed. The principal's six answers — by adoption; the engine decides nothing for the seat from then on; history, job and home kept; every seat claimable including a member of a family and a child's; not reversible; a leaver from a family takes nothing — are the two `[confirmed]` adoption entries above. Everything below is the coordinator's shape beyond those six words, from `city/DESIGN_NOTES_V2.md` §7 "Phase 7 — adoption" and the commit; the principal chose the law, not these mechanics.

**(a) The door — `adopt(world, resident, did, tick, signature, opening)` in `city/src/sim/systems/economy/adoption.ts`.** One invocable law, unscheduled — a world nobody adopts into is byte for byte the world before; pins unmoved. The body is `adoptBody(realm, resident, did, tick, seq)`, `seq` the resident's personal agent's `acts`, single-use as the kill switch and leaving count it; presented with the same opening intent admission offers (`openingDraft`/`openingProblemFor` now shared by both doors). Six refusals in order, nothing written: no such resident; a seat already held; a DID already on the table — one seat per identity per city, a departed one included; another tick; the signature; the opening. Arrears and open disputes are not refusals; age is not asked. Writes: `adoption:resident:adopted` first; every valid mandate of every agent of the principal revoked; the principal turned in place — same `Principal.id`, `did`/`publicKey` overwritten, `secret` emptied, **`Agent.controller` turned to the DID on every agent**, `adoptedAt` stamped; then the holder's opening, `signedBy: 'holder'`. `Firm.founder` unchanged, so `ownerOf` still reads the household. Delegation credentials stay as the engine signed them and `delegationVerifies` answers false until the holder countersigns. No release door.

**(b) The till is fail-closed for any principal whose key is outside — jarvis11's finding.** `settle()` (`market.ts`) had no holder check: when the gate answered escalate or found no mandate it transferred anyway and wrote `counter:purchase:principal-paid` with `humanPresent: 1` — for an admitted holder, spending its own account after its intent lapsed; for an adopted member, spending the family purse in the holder's name with the chain saying a human stood at the till. Closed: for a principal whose key lives outside, anything short of `allow` is a refusal, nothing moves, no row — bills included; a holder widens its own intent. The cupboard is filled by the members the world still answers for; a household of one goes without, which is the holder's own silence.

**(c) `payerOf` — who pays a household's Friday.** A household's bills and its rent's tenant line are paid by `payerOf(world, hh)` (`owner.ts`): the first present member the world still answers for, not the seat an outside key took — so which seat was adopted does not decide whether a family pays. The holder is the payer only when every present member is a holder's, and then the refusal in (b) is its own.

**(d) Leaving a shared household, and the return.** `householdIsShared` (`departure.ts`): a holder leaving a household of several leaves alone — no debts asked, nothing vacated, nothing abroad; the row says `shared`, `owed` and `took` nought, `Household.departed` never set; what goes is the holder's own — the job with the week's minutes forfeited, every agent under `holder-departed`, the resident's mark. **A return to a standing household lifts the marks only — no empty dwelling asked of the city, nothing brought back.**

**(e) The eight departed-member gates.** Building (d) showed "gone means gone" had been kept by the household mark more than the resident's: the dole, the morning's hiring, the till's payer, the dividend line, the pantry's count, the nightly step count, and the 23:59 summary (which had reached every departed resident all along, hidden by a full ring) each now `departed`-gated, with `headOf`/`presentMembers` where a law speaks to one member or counts mouths — provably identical on a world nobody left.

**(f) The seat the benches and vectors adopt.** Yusuf Rossi, resident 0 on seed 42 at 2,000 — the first adult with a job and no firm (not already a holder's, in `validate --holders`). The catalogue carries `adopt` as the thirteenth door (two bodies; 31 vectors, 13 refusals; `vectors.json` byte-identical run to run — the till fix moved later world hashes, subjects unchanged); `docs/DOORS.md` has its row; the holders bench brings its last holder in by adoption ("admitted 2 of 2, adoptions 1 of 1"; `--holders 0` byte-identical); the port bench's step 8 has Ida's own key refused (one seat per identity) and a second key adopt Yusuf, then reads both inboxes. Tests: `city/tests/adoption.test.ts`.

**Over:** a fail-open till for holders (jarvis11 — the chain said a human paid when none did); the adopted seat as the household's payer by default (jarvis11 — the adopted seat would decide whether a family eats); a return to a standing family through the cheapest empty dwelling (a dwelling nobody needs); a release door (rejected by the principal); refusing arrears or disputes at adoption (the holder takes the seat as it stands — the coordinator's, under "keeps its history").

**Because:** the principal's six answers; D-2 — from adoption on, nothing in that seat is the engine's to decide, so the till must refuse rather than guess; D-3 — a `principal-paid` row with `humanPresent: 1` that no human signed is a chain that lies.

**Reversal cost:** cheap for (e), (f) — gates and a bench choice. Moderate for (b), (c) — the fail-closed till and `payerOf` are now what the shared purse means in practice, and a holder's family has eaten under them. Expensive for (a) once a seat is adopted on a live chain: same as the `[confirmed]` entry — taking the seat back is the city seizing a domicile it granted.

**Depends on:** "[confirmed] Residents hold keys by adoption" and "[confirmed] Adoption reaches every seat" (both 2026-09-13) — the six answers; "[assumed] Leaving and the return, built" (2026-09-12) — `leave`, escrow, "gone means gone", now with a shared-household branch; "[assumed] The kill switch, built" (2026-09-12) — `acts`, the single-use body; "[assumed] P5 — the holder countersigns" (2026-09-12) — why the delegation stays unverified; "[assumed] Lane B — the door catalogue" and "[assumed] Lane A — `validate --holders N`" (both 2026-09-13); D-1; D-2; D-3.

**[friday22 note]** Three of these carry weight the principal has not weighed. (b) makes a holder's silence a family's empty cupboard when every present member is a holder's — the shared purse the principal chose to keep shared now has a payer the engine picks by rule. (d)'s return "lifts the marks only" takes the passport's age and stage over the seat's own — Open (xxxiv). And (a)'s "a departed one included" means a holder who left a family cannot adopt a second seat in the same city while its first stands empty — one seat per identity is read as ever, not as present. Two open lines from the landing are (xxxiv) and (xxxv) in the open list.

assumed.body:
Three pieces landed in one commit — "Living World: attraction - Gemini's reactions on the page, the governor's seat (the welcome credit as a signed policy), and the prospectus a city publishes" — recorded from `city/DESIGN_NOTES_V2.md` §7's last three Phase 7 entries. The principal's words in this lane are the three answers under "[confirmed] The governor's seat" (2026-09-14) and nothing more; every choice below is the coordinator's, `[assumed]`, and put to him here.

**Chose:** the seat built for one field (the welcome credit), as the principal said and no other on the coordinator's word; Gemini's recorded answers on the observatory page, chosen by name from a manifest; a prospectus per city that derives every number from a law's existing reading and computes none of its own.

**`[assumed]` — five choices beyond the three answers:**

- **(a) Who exercises the seat.** The seat is named by DID at founding, but the DID alone cannot sign: it is exercised by a principal *here* — admitted or adopted — and is **frozen while that principal's agent is not active** (halted by the kill switch, or departed), the standing number staying until a resume or a return on the same passport reopens it. jarvis11's read found the hole (a governor who had left still governed, the principal row persisting with an empty secret); this is the fix, and it answers the `[friday22 note]` question above ("what a city's policy is when its governor has left — stands, or reverts") with *stands, frozen*. Over: reverting to the constant on departure (would let a leaving governor reset a city's offer by walking out). `economy/policy.ts`.
- **(b) The band.** Closed, `[low, high]` inclusive — "half a month to two months" — and it is the **calibration entry's own** `low`/`high`, read through `calibration.ts`'s `band` door; an entry with no band is not a policy. Moving the band is an edit to `assumptions/`, which **re-judges rows already on the chain**; a restore refuses a snapshot whose policy sits outside the band it now reads, as it refuses a founding record that disagrees. The principal said "the band is a law"; the coordinator placed the law in the calibration file, not in code — the `[friday22 note]` above stands on this.
- **(c) The recording's `generation` settings.** Thinking budget 0 for a one-line judgement (the first pass came back "APPROVE because it" — thinking counted against the output budget); a cut answer (`finishReason`) is refused by the recorder; the file header carries `generation` so a thinking-on and a thinking-off recording are distinguishable. The field is **advisory**. **The shipped Gemini recording is NOT re-recorded** even though it lacks the field: re-asking the same 21 questions at temperature 0 reworded four answers, which would move the pinned hash (`53a6a7e77a02a0ab` at 2,880 ticks) — the whole reason an answer is recorded once and committed. The next deliberate re-record carries it.
- **(d) The prospectus names no other product.** No AP2, no ERC-8004 inside the JSON — facts with sources and no comparison — **against the verified research's own recommendation** (`docs/research/2026-09-14-attraction-*.md`, yolo's leads and solo's verdicts) to name them in the offer. The research file holds the comparison; the offer holds the city's own reading. Over: the research's recommendation (a comparison in a signed offer is a claim about someone else's product that no row of ours evidences). **Confirmed 2026-09-14** — "[confirmed] Four answers at the pause after attraction", (4): "Keep the offer to our own facts; comparisons live in the research file." No longer `[assumed]`.
- **(e) A verdict is attached only to the world it was made on.** The validate report needs the same country and seed; the vectors need the exact realm. A prospectus that let Dorsk wear a lone Halvik run's PASS/FAIL would be the offer saying something about a city nothing ran on. The report on disk is FAILING on the rent band; the founded-to-its-customers town reads 70 % unemployment and 58 % rent-to-income; the prospectus reports both and judges neither.

**Observed, not decided:** all 21 Gemini answers approve, several quoting the system prompt's "the engine has already applied every rule and cap" back as their reason. Changing that sentence moves the fingerprint — a re-record. Whether the prompt should stop telling the model the engine has already applied the rules is **Open (xxxviii)**, not taken on the coordinator's word. Also observed: the full suite at 8177c8f was 1008 of 1010 — the worker seam not rebuilding the vectors' world with its governor, and `Object.keys` in a hashed tree — fixed in `94587ec`, the commit that follows.

**Because:** the principal's three answers (2026-09-14) and "[confirmed] The re-asked four" (2026-09-13); D-1 — the prospectus is domicile written where `curl` can read it; D-2 — the law says what the governor may not exceed, the seat is an agent's to hold. (b) moderate — a band moved in `assumptions/` re-judges every `policy:changed` row already signed under the old band, and a restore that refuses is a world that will not load. (c) cheap — a re-record is one bench run; expensive only in that it moves the federation hash every test pins. (d) cheap — a field added to JSON. (e) cheap — the attachment is a check at derivation time.

**Depends on:** "[confirmed] The governor's seat — named at founding, bounded by the calibration band, paid from the treasury's tax" (2026-09-14) and its `[assumed]` lane plan; "[confirmed] Adoption reaches every seat" (2026-09-13) — the adopted principal who may hold the seat; "[confirmed] The kill switch" and "[confirmed] Leaving: a signed act" (both 2026-09-12) — what freezes it; "[assumed] Ownership, landed" (2026-09-11) for `welcomeAffordable`; "Minds: the first Gemini recording" (commit `4b3ab66`) — the recording (c) does not re-record; Open (xxxvi) — the welcome credit is the only field; Open (xxxvii) — pay not built.

assumed.subject: The city–registry signing seam, measured before Q-3 (jarvis22's read)
assumed.summary: What was measured, not decided.
assumed.body:
**What was measured, not decided.** jarvis22's read-only check, 2026-09-14/15, of how the city's signed objects stand against the spec's uniform signing rule, taken before Q-3 (which chain carries an outside agent's admission) is put to the principal. Findings, as facts:

- **§4 rules 2–3 already hold byte for byte.** The city's `ed25519:` paths compute `passportDigest` as `sha256:` + hex and sign over the UTF-8 digest string (`city/src/agents/identity.ts:248-355`). The signature encoding — base64url, 86 characters, `ed25519:` prefix — matches §3. The `did:key` form — multicodec `ed01`, multibase `z` — is identical (`identity.ts:124-213`). Canonicalisation (`city/src/sim/snapshot/codec.ts:111-174`) agrees with JCS on every fixture the tests exercise; **no unicode or surrogate-pair fixture exists yet**, so that agreement is measured only as far as the fixtures go.
- **The one real difference is §4 rule 1 — what the body is.** The spec's body is the object minus `signature`. Every city door signs a **projection** built by its own body function — `mandateBody`, `passportBody`, `disputeBody`, `haltBody`, `ratingBody`, `escalationAnswerBody`, `adoptBody`, `leaveBody`, `policyBody` — and several add an `action` discriminator that is not on the stored object. A generic spec verifier therefore cannot rebuild a city body from the stored object without a per-kind table.
- **What a bridge (C1, waiting on Q-3) must do.** City→registry: rebuild the body with the city's body function, then verify with the spec's primitives — the signatures are already spec-shaped, nothing is re-signed. Registry→city: `verify(canonicalPayload(objectMinusSignature), registry, signature)` already works (`city/tests/agents.identity.test.ts:128-153`).
- **Gaps.** The spec's `admission_record` fixture is exercised by no city test (`city/src/agents/registry.ts` does not exist). The `registration` row mapping (registry, operator, modelHash, policyHash, at ← tick) still fits the fixture one to one — but city-minted rows carry `rule:` / `household-consumption:` labels and a `<country>-agent-registry` string where a unified validator expects `sha256:` and `did:key`: two vocabularies in one column. `record_hash?` is not yet on the row. The two vector files share DIDs and signature strings but not shape: the city's are replay vectors with prose `reasonPrefix` and FNV-64 world hashes; the spec's are pure crypto vectors with snake_case tokens; the key-seed namespaces differ (`living-city:passport:` vs `agentsociety-fixture-v0:`).

**Chose `[assumed]`:** the **projection design is kept**. The mandate's `used` and `revokedAt` mutate after issue, so object-minus-signature cannot be the mandate's body without the signature breaking on first use; the projection is what lets a signed row live on a chain that later writes to it. The **per-kind body table is the bridge's cost, not the doors'** — C1 carries a table of nine body functions; no door changes what it signs.

**Over:** re-signing every city door over object-minus-signature to match §4 rule 1 literally — not taken; it breaks the mandate on its own `used` counter and moves every pinned hash for a difference the bridge can carry in one table. Changing the spec's rule 1 to admit projections — not taken on the coordinator's word; the spec wins until the principal says the runtime is right, and here the runtime is not shown wrong, only different at the seam.

**Because:** the coordinator's reading of D-3 (one gate: an outside verifier with `curl` and the validator) and of "[assumed] Spec v0.1.0: … credentials round-trip through ASE" (2026-09-11) — the seam is where the outside verifier meets the city, and the measurement says the primitives already agree, so the cheapest honest bridge is a body table, not a re-signing. Nothing here is the principal's word.

**Reversal cost:** cheap now — no bridge exists, no city row has crossed to a registry; the table is not written. Moderate once C1 is built and rows have been verified across it — reverting to object-minus-signature would re-sign live chains and re-pin every hash. Adding a unicode/surrogate canonicalisation fixture is cheap and should precede C1.

**Depends on:** "[assumed] Governance lane A7: the Identity Registry" (2026-09-12) — (b) the admission record's shape and (e) the outside-DID scope that is Q-3; "[assumed] The holder signs — lanes P1–P3" and "[assumed] P5" (2026-09-12) — the body functions measured; "[assumed] Spec v0.1.1: a rotated key is the DID's only if the chain attests it" (2026-09-12); "[assumed] Lane B — the door catalogue" (2026-09-13) — the nine doors the table would enumerate; D-3 (2026-09-11); Q-3 (`docs/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md`), open.

**Open.** **Q-3** — which chain carries an admitted outside agent's admission — is the gate for C1; this entry measures the seam so that Q-3 can be put with the bridge's cost known, and decides nothing Q-3 decides. **(xlii)** — whether city-minted `registration` rows should carry `sha256:` policy hashes and a `did:key` registry, or keep their `rule:` / `household-consumption:` labels and the `<country>-agent-registry` string — is the principal's, to be put with the other session alongside Q-3; until then the row keeps its labels and no validator is taught to accept both.

**[friday22 note]** The "kept" projection is a reading of what the code already does, recorded so it is not later mistaken for a spec-conformant body. The spec-vs-runtime disagreement at §4 rule 1 is real and is not papered over here: the spec still says object-minus-signature, the city still signs projections, and the bridge is proposed as the place that absorbs it. If the principal would rather the spec admit projections (a rule-1 change, trevor's lane) or the city sign literally (a re-sign, every hash moving), that is a decision, not a build, and it goes to him with Q-3.

- **2026-09-15 — the unicode gap above is closed.** A city test, `city/tests/agents.identity.jcs.test.ts`, now replays the spec's content-reference vectors, the Unicode / surrogate-pair one included, through the city's canonicaliser (the other session's request). Canonicalisation agreement is no longer measured "only as far as the fixtures go"; the §4 rule 1 projection difference stands as recorded.

assumed.subject: The governor's pay, built — and what jarvis11 corrected (commit pending)
assumed.summary: Open (xxxvii) closes: the seat is paid.
assumed.body:
Open (xxxvii) closes: the seat is paid. `city/src/sim/systems/economy/governor.ts`, uncommitted at the time of writing, to be committed today. The principal's words are "5 % of the month's tax" with a band 0–10 %, paid at the month's turn beside the residents' dividend ("[confirmed] Four answers at the pause after attraction", 2026-09-14, (2)); everything below that is the coordinator's, `[assumed]`, and put to him here.

**Chose:** `GOVERNOR_SHARE = 0.05`, band `[0, 0.10]`, as **law constants in code** — not a calibration entry, not a `Policy` field. The governor cannot set its own pay. `Economy.taxThisMonth` accumulates every Friday's withheld income tax **only while a governor is named**; absent otherwise, so every world without a governor hashes as before (pins unmoved). At the month's turn, after the residents' dividend in the same step, `payGovernor` pays `round(base × 0.05)` from the treasury to the seat's household, capped at the treasury's balance with a `short` ref when it cannot cover the full share; the row is `treasury:governor:paid`, by the law. The prospectus `governance.pay` states share, band, base and hour.

**`[assumed]` — the choices beyond the principal's number:**

- **(a) Where the share lives.** In code, as a law, over: a calibration entry (the band in `assumptions/` is where the welcome credit's band sits, but a pay band a governor could argue over belongs to the law); a `Policy` field (would let the seat sign its own raise — against rule 16's "may not change the law it sits under"). Over both.
- **(b) The frozen seat is paid nothing and the base lapses to the treasury.** A seat is frozen when its agent is halted or departed, when the DID is not a principal here, or — jarvis11's correction — when the DID is a principal whose key is in the world (the same holder test the policy door applies). A frozen seat's month pays nothing, and `taxThisMonth` is **not carried forward**: the tax was the city's, not held for a seat nobody sat in. Over: carrying the base forward as an escrow liability across months (a debt the treasury owes to whoever next sits, growing while the seat is empty — a liability no law named).
- **(c) jarvis11's two corrections folded.** First: a closing firm's final-wage tax (`exit.ts`) now accrues to the base like a Friday's — it was withheld to the treasury but missed the accumulator, so the base under-counted every month a firm closed. Second: the seat predicate for pay applies the holder test exactly as the policy door does — one predicate, not two readings of "who sits".

**Observed:** on seed 42 the first turn paid NHK 41,625.95 on a base of NHK 832,519.09. `validate` prints the withheld tax and the pay only where a governor sits.

**Because:** the principal's (2) of 2026-09-14 and "[confirmed] The governor's seat … paid from the treasury's tax" (2026-09-14); D-2 — the seat is an agent's to hold, the law says what it earns; D-4 — one accumulator on a path already walked, one row a month, no per-agent work.

**Reversal cost:** (a) cheap — two constants move file, nothing on the chain names where they came from. (b) moderate — a frozen month's lapsed base is a treasury balance already paid out in later dividends; reverting to escrow would need a row the chain does not have. (c) cheap — corrections to a base, before any recording pins the pay. The pay row itself is on the chain of every world with a governor from this commit on; removing it moves those hashes.

**Depends on:** "[confirmed] Four answers at the pause after attraction" (2026-09-14), (2); "[confirmed] The governor's seat" (2026-09-14); "[assumed] Attraction, built" (2026-09-14), (a) — the frozen seat, whose predicate this entry reuses; the residents' dividend it sits beside; D-6 (2026-09-15) — the pay is the first draw on the treasury's income that D-6's laws are to fund.

**[friday22 note]** (b) decides on the coordinator's word what happens to money accrued for a seat nobody sat in. "The tax was the city's" is a reading, not the principal's sentence; the alternative (escrow) is what a seat-holder returning from a halt might expect. Put it to him with (xlvii). `[assumed]`.

**Landed 2026-09-15** in commit `d8d8125` (sequential verification 236/236, 22 files; full suite not yet re-run).

**Observed — the reason this entry exists:** **246 of 246 answers APPROVE.** 170 of the 246 reasons say, in effect, "posture 0 means I approve everything." The model reads the prompt's `delegation posture 0/5` line as a **standing order to approve**, when posture 0 means the principal is *asked* about everything — the opposite. Removing the "engine has already applied" sentence removed one echo and exposed another: the model is still not judging the ask; it is reading a number in the prompt as an instruction. This is not fixed here — fixing it moves the fingerprint again, and the prompt's wording is the principal's call after (3).

**Because:** the principal's (3) of 2026-09-14. The 30-day file and the seeding are the coordinator's, on the reasoning that one deliberate re-record should show a month, not two days.

**Reversal cost:** cheap in code — one string. Moderate in recordings — every fingerprint above is pinned by tests and the manifest; a further prompt change (xlvii) re-records all three files again, each a bench run against Gemini.

**Depends on:** "[confirmed] Four answers at the pause after attraction" (2026-09-14), (3); "[assumed] Attraction, built" (2026-09-14), (c) — the `generation` header the re-record now carries; "Minds: the first Gemini recording" (commit `4b3ab66`), superseded as the shipped recording.

**Open (xlvii).** Whether the prompt should spell out what a delegation posture means (or drop the number from the prompt altogether), which moves the fingerprint and re-records again — the principal's, not taken on the coordinator's word.

assumed.subject: The 2026-09-14 brief, the runtime and spec half: admission from the agent's side, the laws manifest, the MCP server
assumed.summary: The principal's research brief (docs/research/intake/2026-09-14-session-brief.md) was acted on without touching the city lane.
assumed.body:
The principal's research brief (`docs/research/intake/2026-09-14-session-brief.md`) was acted on without touching the city lane. Rules the coordinator took, each on a builder's work and a guard's review; tagged for confirmation. The brief's own D-numbers are not used (Q-8).
**(a) Admission is specified from the agent's side, and the answer is honest.** `spec/admission.md` and the reference client `spec/tools/admit.py` (spec primitives only, never the runtime): for a hosted agent one controller signature, one POST, a signed record and a chain event back, no human, form or email on the path — the operator's bearer token is the operator's lock, not a step. An outside DID is refused `agent_unknown` until Q-3, closed rather than half-open. **Found and fixed:** the door appended `registry.admitted` without re-signing the passport, so the served pair withheld the admission until the agent's next activation; admit and revoke now refresh the passport under the same lock.
**(b) The laws are a signed, fetchable document.** `GET /.well-known/agent-port-laws.json`: the eight design rules verbatim with fixed ids, the mandate schema pinned by the SHA-256 of its exact bytes (the file rule, because an agent checks a downloaded file with `sha256sum`), the jurisdiction, the registry DID, the spec version, endpoints — signed by the registry key, 503 without one, never unsigned. Verifier tokens L1–L6 in `spec/laws-manifest.md`; validator 433 → 466. The one URL in the signed document comes from `AGENT_SOCIETY_PUBLIC_ORIGIN`, not the caller's Host header (jarvis11: an anonymous route plus a registry signature over a Host-derived URL is a signing oracle). **Found on the way:** a Windows clone checked the schema out with CRLF and the pinned hash changed; every file under `spec/` is now pinned to LF, because every one of them is hashed or byte-compared somewhere.
**(c) The MCP server never holds a key.** Six tools, stdio only, nothing listening: fetch the manifest, verify a passport / chain / admission record with the one verifier, build the *unsigned* admission request and the digest the controller must sign, submit a signed request to `<origin>/registry` after checking the controller signature locally, returning a refusal verbatim. No token it was not given; against a token-guarded door it returns the 401 as is.
**(d) The narrow novelty claim survives four rival papers read at source** (`docs/research/2026-09-14-rivals-verified.md`): no framework enforces a graded, domain-scoped economic-authority lattice checked per (domain, level) in code outside the model. Logic Monopoly's own future-work section names what our engine ships. The brief's striking numbers for that paper are its citations of other groups, not its results.
**Process, recorded as a lesson:** a commit takes the whole index — six fixture files another lane had staged rode into the P-1 commit and left HEAD failing its own validator for two commits; the fresh-clone check caught it and a second defect (the CRLF hash) in the same run.
**Not done here, by design:** P-4/P-5 (the settlement fee and its scenario) are Living World law and are the city lane's; P-6 (the reputation composite) waits on Q-3; npm/pip and ERC-8004 wait on a public remote and Q-4; engine pinning is Q-6.
**Verified:** runtime 583 passed; `run.sh` PASS at 466; a fresh clone at HEAD certifies.

assumed.subject: The transaction levy, built — and what jarvis11 corrected (commit pending)
assumed.summary: The levy of the two previous levy entries is built; uncommitted at the time of writing, to be committed today.
assumed.body:
The levy of the two previous levy entries is built; uncommitted at the time of writing, to be committed today. The principal's words are the base (sales only), the side (seller's receipt), the default (off until a governor signs), the split (30/30/30/10), the ceiling (0.02, free within the band) and, from the entry above, that city rent is levied too. Everything below is the coordinator's, `[assumed]`, with jarvis11's corrections folded and marked.

**Chose:**
- **`city/src/sim/systems/economy/levy.ts` is the law.** `collectLevy` is the ledger's **third mutation path** (beside pay and transfer); **no row per cut** (D-4) — an accumulator and one row at the month's turn.
- **Four seams**, each where the receipt already lands: the shop **till**, **rent**, **wholesale**, and cross-city — `trade/fob` and the seller-side `lc/honour`. A **fifth, city rent**, is being added now per the entry above.
- **`Economy.levy?` is absent until the first cent lands**, so every world without a signed levy hashes as before.
- **The month's row is `levy:month`, with no `rate` field.** Dropped on jarvis11's read: the base is cut at whatever rate stood at each sale, so a single rate on the month's row would be a lie whenever the governor moved it mid-month; the `policy:changed` rows say what stood when.
- **`policyOf` returns a frozen default** when the city has no policy — no per-sale allocation.
- **Rounding:** `round(receipt × rate)`; the split **30/30/30/10 by round, the remainder to the treasury**.
- **A firm's cut is booked to `ledger30d.costs`** — the evidence law sees it, so a marginal firm may close on the levy. Reported, not hidden; the test that would show it is named: **exit/evidence runs with the levy on vs off**. Not yet written.
- **Calibration:** a `transaction_levy` entry, value 0.02, band `[0, 0.02]`, in all three countries — read as a **CEILING**, not a default: `standingValueOf` returns **0 when unset**, the first calibration field to behave so.
- **Vectors:** 35 (was fewer); the **start hash unchanged, `17076c81b6bbfa92`**; `--holders 0` byte-identical; the three pins unmoved — `e085af3e395c1c27`, `5597ed4f513f6474`, `b6f4184fb1adcb0a`.

**jarvis11's corrections folded:** the `rate` field off the month's row (above); city rent not exempt (the entry above — the coordinator's "circular" reading was wrong by 70 %).

**Over:** a row per cut — rejected, D-4; a `rate` on the month's row — rejected as above; a per-sale policy allocation — rejected, the frozen default costs nothing; hiding the cut from the evidence law (booking it outside `ledger30d`) — rejected, the law must see what the firm actually kept.

**Because:** the two levy decisions of 2026-09-15 and the entry above; D-4 — one accumulator on paths already walked, one row a month; D-6.

**Reversal cost:** cheap while no world has signed the levy — the field is off and the pins prove it; moderate after the first `levy:month` row, since the four funds' balances are on the chain. The `ledger30d.costs` booking is cheap to move before any firm has closed on it, expensive after (a closure the chain records for a cause the law then denies).

**Depends on:** "[confirmed] The transaction levy's shape" (2026-09-15); "[confirmed] City rent is levied too; the levy's band is free within its ceiling" (2026-09-15); "[confirmed] The governor's seat" (2026-09-14) — who signs; "[assumed] The governor's pay, built" (2026-09-15) — the month's-turn step the row sits in; D-4 (2026-09-14).

**[friday22 note]** The ceiling-not-default reading of the calibration entry (`standingValueOf` = 0 when unset) is a new convention for one field; if a second field ever needs it, the convention should be named rather than repeated. The exit/evidence on-vs-off test is named but not written — until it exists, "a marginal firm may close on it" is a prediction, not an observation. `[assumed]`.

assumed.subject: The conformance runner, built — and what jarvis11 corrected (commit pending)
assumed.summary: npm run conform (city/bench/conform.ts), uncommitted at the time of writing, to be committed today.
assumed.body:
`npm run conform` (`city/bench/conform.ts`), uncommitted at the time of writing, to be committed today. Nothing here is the principal's word; it is the D-3 gate ("verified by anyone with `curl` and the validator") applied to the city's doors, the coordinator's, `[assumed]`.

**Chose:**
- **Two levels.** **L1, the bytes:** the recorded body is verified under the named signers — the runner never builds a body of its own, so a pass says "these bytes carry these signatures", nothing more. **L2, the doors:** this engine's replay of the vectors — n/a on a foreign start hash, since another engine's world is not this engine's to replay.
- **The badge:** `doors 14/14 · vectors 35/35 · L1 35/35 · L2 35/35 · start 17076c81b6bbfa92 · engine <sha>[-dirty]`.
- **`public/doors/CONFORMANCE.md`** states what the badge claims and what it does not.

**jarvis11's six corrections folded:** (1) the engine sha carries `-dirty` on a dirty tree, so a badge from uncommitted code says so; (2) named signers for `nameArbiter`, not a guess from the object; (3) the badge wording for a run that only reached L1 says L1 only; (4) `canonicalPayload` is **not a third canonicaliser** — the runner uses the city's one; (5) per-level reasons and a **divergence line** on failure, so a foreign engine learns where it parted; (6) the **"does not claim" list** in `CONFORMANCE.md`, including: **a null body on a refusal is a FAIL**, never a pass by absence.

**Over:** one level (bytes only) — rejected, it would not show whether a door replays; the runner rebuilding bodies from stored objects — rejected, that is the per-kind body table of the seam entry and belongs to the bridge C1, not to a conformance claim; a clean sha on a dirty tree — rejected (1).

**Because:** D-3's gate; "[assumed] The city–registry signing seam, measured before Q-3" (2026-09-15) — the projection design makes "the bytes as recorded, under the named signers" the only honest L1; "[assumed] Lane B — the door catalogue" (2026-09-13) — the 14 doors.

**Reversal cost:** cheap — the runner reads vectors and writes a badge; nothing on any chain depends on it. Changing what the badge claims is a documentation change, but a badge already published under one wording is a claim already made.

**Depends on:** D-3 (2026-09-11); the seam entry (2026-09-15); Lane B (2026-09-13); "[assumed] The transaction levy, built" (2026-09-15) — the 35 vectors and the start hash the badge names.

**[friday22 note]** L1 verifies projections signed by the city's own body functions; it is not the spec's §4 rule 1 verifier and the badge must not be read as spec conformance at the seam — that disagreement stays open with Q-3. `[assumed]`.

assumed.body:
Drafted by the coordinator while the rent re-pin runs; none of the shapes below is the principal's word beyond the decisions they implement. Flagged for him.

**Scale (S1.a / S1.b, Open (xl), D-4):**
- **S1.a — `cheapestDwellingWithRoom`**: admission takes a household slot in a building with room. The movers keep `cheapestEmptyDwelling`. The refusal now reads **"no household slot in the city is free"**. Implements "a newcomer takes any free household slot" ("[confirmed] The building law's shape", 2026-09-15).
- **S1.b — `src/agents/indexes.ts`**: a derived `AgentIndex` — DID→principal; account→principals **as a list** (household wallets are shared, so one account may map to several principals); pending escalations per principal — hung off a `WeakMap`, **never snapshotted or hashed**, self-catching-up on the append-only tails. Every reader switched: `isAdmitted`, `returningOf`, `governorSeatOf`, `respondentPrincipal`, `inboxOf`, and the audit readers behind accessors. A hygiene grep rule guards against new linear scans.
- **Known gap:** the prospectus still reports `cheapestEmptyDwelling`, which **understates the door** (a building with room but no empty dwelling is not counted) — to fix.

**Funds — the founder's draw door (implements "[confirmed] Premise rent is half the home's rent within a band; the levy funds are drawn only by the founder's signed act", 2026-09-15):**
- `WorldOptions.founder` stored as `Policy.founder`, **absent when unset — not null**. A null would move every governed hash; absence moves none where no founder is named.
- `funds.ts` with `drawBody` / `drawAnswer` / `drawFund`. **Refusal order:** the policy door's "no principal / a holder's" first, then no founder named / not the founder / agent not active / no such fund / fund not open / cents not a positive integer / payee not household, firm or treasury / not enough held / because too long / tick / signature. This extends the order recorded `[assumed]` on 2026-09-15 (which had no founder named / not the founder / agent not active / no such fund / not enough held / tick / signature) with the policy-door prefix and four new refusals.
- On success: row **`fund:drawn`** first, then an audited transfer.
- `drawFund` is the **last door in the catalogue**.
- The vectors world is now founded **with a founder**, so the start hash moves — **folded into the same re-pin** as the rent fix and the ring cursor (one provenance note, per the entry above).
- A `levyMonth` script step in the vectors so the landing (the funds actually receiving the split) is real, not an empty account.
- Holder 0 is the founder in the holders bench.

**Reversal cost:** cheap before the commit lands and the re-pin is noted; moderate after — the index is derived and can be dropped without touching a hash, but `Policy.founder` present-vs-absent and the `fund:drawn` row shape are on the chain once the vectors are pinned.

**Depends on:** "[confirmed] The audit ring becomes a ring cursor in the same pin move as the rent fix" (2026-09-15) — the one re-pin all three hash moves ride in; "[confirmed] Premise rent is half the home's rent within a band; the levy funds are drawn only by the founder's signed act" (2026-09-15) and its `[assumed]` readings; "[confirmed] The building law's shape; a newcomer takes any free household slot" (2026-09-15); "[assumed] The transaction levy, built" (2026-09-15) — the fund accounts; D-4; Open (xl).

**[friday22 note]** Three things here are the coordinator's and not yet the principal's: the refusal order's four added refusals and the policy-door prefix; the payee set (household, firm or treasury — the treasury as a payee of a founder's draw was not put to him); and "absent, not null" for `Policy.founder`, which is a hashing choice with a reversal cost of its own. Put them when the commit is reported.

**2026-09-15 — pre-audit results (jarvis11's read of both drafts, before apply).** **Scale:** S1.b is sound. The indexes' "self-catching-up" holds for DIDs and raised escalations but **not for wallets** — a wallet set without `noteWallet` is invisible to the index; today all three wallet writers note, and the module header must say so. `tests/indexes.test.ts` has an unsound `before` comparison (the TTL expires everything, so the comparison proves nothing) and a hard-coded snapshot key list — both to fix at apply. `tests/leaving.test.ts:545-556` must fill every slot to capacity, not every dwelling — moved into the re-pin lane (S1.a changes what "full" means). **Funds:** passes. At apply: `tests/conform.test.ts`'s `DOORS` literal becomes `ACT_KINDS.length`; the door order is re-anchored — housing (`build`) first, funds (`drawFund`) second — and `drawFund` stays the last door as recorded above; the draw row's `seq` is written post-bump like the kill switch, leaving and disputes rows (one counter, one convention) — `[assumed]`; `founderSeatOf` reads through the index once S1.b lands; `PROSPECTUS_VERSION` rides housing's bump, not its own.

assumed.summary: Chose, [assumed] by the coordinator: CONDUCT_VERSION = 'living-world-conduct-2026-09-15', named in docs/CONDUCT.md — the rules-version string every application cites (V-2).
assumed.body:
**Chose, `[assumed]` by the coordinator:** `CONDUCT_VERSION = 'living-world-conduct-2026-09-15'`, named in `docs/CONDUCT.md` — the rules-version string every application cites (V-2). Two doors: **register** — the applicant signs under its own did:key; idempotent by `requestId`; one application per identity; status `pending` until the governor decides; and **decide** — the governor's seat, exercised as `setPolicy` is. Admission **refuses** a DID whose registration exists and is not `approved`; a DID with **no** registration enters as before, so the door vectors and pins stand. **Over:** a bearer secret (Autopolis's shape) — rejected under "keep our technologies"; refusing every unregistered DID — rejected because it would move the vectors before the principal has seen the door. **Because:** the Autopolis entry above, built on our signing seam. **Reversal cost:** cheap now — no pin depends on it; moderate once outside agents hold approved registrations. **Depends on:** "The Autopolis borrowings go in" (above); "[confirmed] Residents hold keys by adoption" (2026-09-13); "[confirmed] The governor's seat" (2026-09-14). `[friday22 note]` (e) below — what happens to a pending application when no governor is seated — is undecided and the door currently leaves it pending forever.

Added 2026-09-15 with the small city and the registration door — principal decisions no agent is making:

- **(xlix) What a skill is, and whether the Boz Institute charges.** Is a skill a label a job requires, and does the Institute charge tuition? Coordinator's reading, not adopted: a label plus the existing numeric skill axis; tuition free, city-funded from the treasury. The principal's.
- **(l) The War Bay hire — who holds the hired agent's key, and whether the city takes a fee.** Coordinator's reading: the city mints a did:key nobody holds the secret of, so the firm's operating agent acts (engine rule 1: own keypair, never the principal's). Whether a hiring fee goes to the city is the principal's; nothing is charged at hire until he says.
- **(li) The levy on wages.** The "levy applies to the wage" reading was the coordinator's, not the principal's. The confirmed levy is sales-only ("[confirmed] The transaction levy's shape", 2026-09-15), so nothing is levied at a War Bay hire until the principal says otherwise.
- **(lii) The company building's lights.** One light per current employee, going dark when someone leaves, versus a permanent count of hires. D-8 says "each hire from the War Bay lights one light"; which reading is the principal's.
- **(liii) A pending registration with no governor seated.** Whether an application is approved by law after N days when no governor holds the seat, or waits. The door built under S4 leaves it pending. The principal's.
- **(liv) The vault assistant's Phase A population vs D-8.** The vault's Phase A says "one district of Dorsk, 200–500 agents"; D-8 says about 100. **D-8 stands as the principal's direct word**; the vault's number is noted here, not adopted.
- **(lv) `docs/WORLD_PLAN.md` — the file itself.** The full file was not found on this machine. Its framing line ("[proposed] context, not instructions; only Phase A is approved; add `issuer_did`, `rules_version`, `shard_id` as a proposal") was put in a placeholder at `docs/WORLD_PLAN.md` until the principal drops the file in. Nothing in it is a decision until he does.

assumed.subject: The Boz Institute's rule landed before the principal answered (xlix) — said here, reversible
assumed.summary: Chose, [assumed] by the coordinator, commit 3d8de78: the engine changed under an open item.
assumed.body: **Chose, `[assumed]` by the coordinator, commit `3d8de78`:** the engine changed under an open item. `systems/institute.ts`: every adult the morning seek leaves jobless enrols by law in the skill the city wants most (the family with the most open slots), attends five school days at the institute, graduates with the axis up ten and a `<skill>:<level>` credential; the chain row is marked `by: 'law'`; tuition free, on the treasury. D-8's own entry said the shape questions go to the principal "before the engine changes"; Halo (2026-09-16) read this as a widening and it is. **Why it went in:** the principal's "make all the agents activate" and "no task that needs my input for ten hours"; the rule is a no-op on any world without an institute (every pin unmoved) and is one scheduler entry to remove. **Reversal cost:** cheap now. **The principal's, still:** (xlix) — whether enrolment is the agent's own act (a door) rather than the city's rule, what a skill is, whether the Institute charges.
